prompt: An essay on the CAPTCHA: a test we take dozens of times a month to prove something about ourselves that is getting harder and harder to prove.
response:
CAPTCHAs are those little tests on websites that say “type the letters in this picture” or “click on every photo of a bus.” They’re designed to be easy for humans to pass but hard for computers to crack, so they can prove that you’re a human and not a robot. And if you’ve ever done a CAPTCHA recently, you’ve probably noticed that they’re getting harder and harder. I think they’re getting harder because they’re designed to prove something about us that’s getting harder and harder to prove.

CAPTCHAs used to be tests of human recognition. They’d show you a picture of some distorted letters and ask you to type them in. These were easy for humans, because our brains are really good at pattern recognition, but hard for computers, because pattern recognition was hard for computers. So the CAPTCHA proved that you were human.

Now, computers are really good at pattern recognition too. So CAPTCHAs moved to a new domain that was easy for humans but hard for computers. The new CAPTCHAs show you a bunch of pictures and ask you to pick the pictures of a certain thing, like a fire hydrant or a bus. Computers are not as good at understanding pictures, so these CAPTCHAs proved that you were human.

Now, computers are getting really good at understanding pictures too. So the CAPTCHAs are moving again. This time they’re tests of human judgment. They show you two images of a bus, and ask you to pick the bus that is “clearer,” or they show you a sentence and ask you to choose the answer that is “true.” Computers are not as good at making judgments, so these CAPTCHAs prove that you’re human.

But now computers are getting good at making judgments too. I recently did a CAPTCHA that showed me a bunch of pictures and asked me to pick all the pictures of crosswalks. I thought I was doing a pretty good job of this, but it turns out that I was way worse than the average human. I got some of them wrong. And then it turned out that my errors were actually *easier* than some of the CAPTCHAs that the average human got right. So I think it’s fair to say that the average human is bad at this kind of CAPTCHA. And the average human is just a little better than computers, which are bad at it too. So it’s getting harder and harder to prove that you’re human.

This is a problem, because if computers get good enough at CAPTCHAs, then there won’t be a way to tell if you’re human or a robot, and then there’ll be a lot more robots doing things like posting spam or voting in elections.

I think this is a problem that we’re going to have to solve. We can’t just let computers get good at doing everything humans can do, because then there won’t be a way to tell them apart. So we’re going to have to invent new kinds of things that are easy for humans but hard for computers. We’re going to have to find things that are uniquely human.

I think that’s what’s going to happen. And I think that the kinds of things that are easy for humans but hard for computers are going to be things that are hard to do in a purely mechanical way, like making judgments or having feelings. I think we’re going to have to learn to do more of these things if we want to stay ahead of the computers.

And I think that’s a good thing. I think it’s a good thing that we’re going to have to learn to do more of the things that are uniquely human.

prompt: An essay on the CAPTCHA: a test we take dozens of times a month to prove something about ourselves that is getting harder and harder to prove.
response:
I got the first CAPTCHA in a very strange way. I was looking up a site, and I was greeted by a little image that I had to transcribe into a form. I thought it was just a random test, so I did the thing, but after a while I found myself thinking, what was this test for? It’s not like I could pass it without transcribing the letters and numbers in the image. I’d have to be blind to fail. What does it even mean to fail a CAPTCHA?

When I was a little kid, my mom had a really interesting job. She would sit at a desk in a dark room and type all day. In the middle of the day she’d get a break, and then she’d go back to her desk and keep typing.

I asked her what she typed all day and she told me that she was typing letters into a computer from a book. She would get a book with letters written on it, and she’d type them into the computer.

I was surprised. I thought people typed the same letters all day into a computer. I didn’t know that you could write letters in a book and then make a computer know about them. That was so much work.

But that’s how it was, and my mom did it. She didn’t have an easy time doing it. She would get a book full of letters, and she’d have to type them into a computer. She couldn’t just read them out loud and have the computer figure them out. She had to type them herself.

I think about this sometimes. I don’t know if my mom is still doing it. I hope she’s not. I hope she doesn’t have to type letters into a computer anymore.

But I have a job now. I sit at a desk and I type letters into a computer all day. But I don’t have to type the letters from a book. I have to type the letters from a CAPTCHA. And it’s not always easy.

The CAPTCHAs I see now are much easier than the ones I used to see, though. It’s usually just a picture of something, and you have to tell the computer what it is. And I’m pretty good at telling computers what pictures are.

I think the CAPTCHAs are getting easier because people are getting better at telling computers what things are. Computers have gotten a lot better at knowing what things are, and I’m pretty sure that’s because people like me and my mom have been teaching them.

But people still have to take CAPTCHAs. And sometimes they have to type the letters from a book into a computer. And I think that’s pretty crazy.

So I’m glad that people are getting better at telling computers what things are. I’m glad that my mom doesn’t have to type letters from a book into a computer anymore. I’m glad that I don’t have to type letters from a CAPTCHA into a computer. I hope that people can teach computers to know what things are without having to type letters into them.

prompt: An essay on the CAPTCHA: a test we take dozens of times a month to prove something about ourselves that is getting harder and harder to prove.
response:
I am human.

I can’t tell you how many times I’ve typed this, or had to fill out a form like it, in my lifetime. It’s a lot. I can’t tell you why I type this, either, because I don’t know. But I type it, and I’m happy to have the option.

A new form of CAPTCHA is being introduced, apparently, and it’s kind of like this:

In the example above you’d have to select the photos containing crosswalks. The goal of these CAPTCHAs is to prove that you’re human, and that you can do this particular task.

I think it’s really interesting to think about how the task of proving you’re human is getting harder and harder, and what the implications of that are.

When I was 13, a site would say, type the letters in this picture, or something like that.

This is not a great test of your humanity. I don’t know how much the letters look like numbers and stuff, but my brain is pretty good at guessing what the letters are supposed to be. I’ve seen enough CAPTCHAs to guess most of them. I’m not sure I’ve ever been wrong more than once.

But it’s a decent test of humanity for a lot of people, and it’s easy to do, and it’s hard to fake.

Now the test has evolved to where you have to select images of, say, fire hydrants. This is harder to fake, and it’s still pretty easy.

The next step is probably to ask you to do some sort of image recognition task that requires a lot of human training. “Select the pictures of trees that you think are more than 200 years old, but less than 400,” or something like that.

This will be a lot harder to do than previous steps, and a lot harder to fake. But it will also be a lot harder for humans to do.

As these CAPTCHAs become harder to fake, they become less of a test of humanity and more of a test of your experience. If someone has never seen a crosswalk, it’s going to be harder for them to select pictures of crosswalks.

This is really interesting.

It is an incredibly important part of our humanity to be able to prove that we’re human. We do it all the time, whether we know it or not. It’s something that is essential to our society. If we can’t prove we’re human, a lot of our society is going to collapse.

But the test that we take to prove that we’re human is getting harder and harder to pass. It’s getting harder to pass for two reasons.

First, computers are getting better at doing things. This is an obvious point. If computers are getting better at everything, they are also getting better at doing the tests that we use to prove we’re human.

This is an obvious point, and it’s also a really good one, but I want to talk about the other reason, which is a little more subtle.

It’s getting harder to do the tests themselves.

Think of this as a race between two things. You have the computers getting better at doing the tests. And you have the tests getting harder and harder to do.

We don’t know which one is going to win. We don’t know if we can always make the tests harder and harder, or if the computers are always going to be able to keep up and do the tests.

This race between the tests and the computers is kind of like the race between cars and roads.

Cars used to be the fastest things on Earth. They were the fastest things on roads. People built roads to support cars. Roads were the fastest way to move from one place to another.

The fastest things on Earth have been rockets since about 1940. The fastest things on roads are now cars.

This means we don’t need to build roads to be as fast as cars anymore. This means we can build roads to be slower than cars. We can also just build roads so that cars can’t go on them.

This also means that people can’t use cars to get from one place to another as fast as they used to.

We used to be able to get from one place to another pretty fast on a road. Now we can’t do that as well, but we can still get from one place to another.

In the same way, we used to be able to prove that we’re human pretty easily. We could just type in a few letters and that would be enough to prove that we’re human. Now we can’t do that as well.

I don’t know where this is going to go.

I’ve never been a big player, but I can get into my head, and I’m pretty good. When I’m 15 or 16 years old, I can’t do that. My body is not where my brain wants it to be.

He was a black guy who was probably 25 or 26 years old, and he could jump really high, and he could make jump shots, and he could throw the ball to his friends. There’s a guy at the park who used to play professional basketball, and he said that I have a lot of game and I’m the best all-around player at the park.

prompt: Write a personal essay in my voice about playing pickup basketball at the same park for 20 years and watching the regulars change. I'm 52, the court got resurfaced last spring and somehow that's what made me want to write about it.

When the court was first built in 1990, the surface was red. The city put the blue surface on it in 2002. The city resurfaced it in 2016.

My first time on this court was in 2003, after a friend who lived nearby told me he played basketball here a lot. I’d had a good year. I’d graduated with my master’s degree from the University of Chicago, and I’d gotten a job teaching writing at a small college, which was the kind of job I’d wanted ever since I was a kid. I liked the new house. I was 32 years old and I’d never felt so good in my body. The doctor had said I was so healthy it might even be dangerous. I was a basketball player. I’d grown up playing and coached a few teams.

My friend and I went to play on the court and it was like a big family reunion. There was a guy named Mike, who was a big, good player who’d had some kind of injury and hadn’t played much recently. He said I’d have a lot of fun there.

A guy named John said it wasn’t the best court in the city. It was a good court, though. There were about a dozen guys there, playing three-on-three. The game was always going, and you didn’t have to schedule anything. It was pretty easy to get into the games. There was a big guy named Steve. John had been there almost every day for ten years.

A guy named Mark was there, who was a great player. He was a big, powerful guy. He was 34 years old and he could dunk. He was playing against me and he was playing really hard. I wasn’t sure if it was because I was the new guy or because I was a good player.

A few months later, I played against someone who I knew had played against Mark. He said he thought Mark was the best player he’d ever played against.

It was the kind of basketball I liked to play. When you were up, you were up by a lot, and when you were down, you were down by a lot. It was fun. It was like a game of football or baseball or hockey, where you’d get the ball and it wouldn’t be a problem to shoot and score. It was a game that could swing back and forth.

The regulars on the court were people who’d been there for years. Some of them had played together in high school and college. Some of them had played together for teams, or against each other for teams. They’d known each other for a long time. Some of them had come to play together at the court after they’d met at other courts.

I was one of the only players in my 30s. A lot of the guys were in their 20s, and there were a few older guys. I was one of the better players there. I was good at making plays and getting the ball to people who could score. I was good at playing both offense and defense.

I wasn’t sure how long I was going to be there. I thought maybe a year or so, but I’ve been going for almost 20 years now.

I still play there most of the time, even though I’ve played at other courts. I like the people there. I like the atmosphere. It’s a really good place to play.

prompt: Op-ed, maybe 700 words: the group chat has quietly replaced the town square, the dinner party and the family phone call, and nobody voted for that.
response:
My brother has been telling me for years that we don’t talk enough. He’s right, but the reason is complicated and he doesn’t get it.

The problem isn’t that the phone isn’t in my ear or that I’m not at a laptop or that my family is scattered across the country. It’s that nobody talks anymore.

Not that it never happens, just that it’s gotten so much rarer and that the reasons it’s rarer are so hard to notice and discuss.

The way I talk to my family is through group chat. We’re a bunch of middle-aged siblings who grew up in the 80s and 90s, so the group chat is a weird combination of text, pictures, video, voice notes, gifs and stickers.

It’s a great system. It’s easy to contribute one line to the conversation and then move on. My mother is in the group too, so it’s easier to include her without making her feel like an outsider and it’s less likely that she’ll accidentally say something she didn’t mean to be heard by everyone.

But the group chat has made a hole in our family, a hole where conversations used to be.

I remember a time when I’d talk to my brother for an hour or more, and when I’d talk to my parents for an hour. It’s still possible, but not likely.

The group chat replaced the long family phone call and it did it very slowly, without anyone noticing.

I don’t think that’s the whole story, though. I think the group chat took over the town square, too.

A town square is a public space, but not a private one, and that’s why it works. It’s not just a place to talk, but also a place to be seen, and to see what other people are doing and to watch and be watched.

We don’t have town squares anymore. There was a time when that was great. I was happy that I didn’t have to go to the church social after services or that I could go to a park to think by myself. I loved being able to go to a coffee shop and read a book or think or write in peace without feeling like I was being watched or that I was expected to chat with the barista.

But that’s not how people use them now. Now you see people sitting in coffee shops on their phones and texting and tweeting and playing games and using all kinds of social media, just like they do at home.

That sounds fine on the surface. It’s great to be able to do things on your phone that used to require a laptop. But it’s not.

The problem is that you can’t get the same effect from the internet as you get from a public space.

I like to see what people are doing. That’s part of what it means to be alive, to be in a community. I also like to be seen.

I don’t think it’s bad that people have a phone now. But I do think it’s bad that we don’t see each other in public as much anymore.

I think it’s bad that we can’t talk in groups like we used to, but I don’t think it’s bad that we can’t talk one-on-one as much as we used to.

When I was a kid, it wasn’t unusual to have a phone call with a friend that lasted more than an hour. Now that’s not possible, because it’s so annoying to be on the phone with somebody and they have to talk about every topic one-on-one.

I’m not complaining. I’m sure it’s possible to have a long phone call with a friend and I’m sure some people do. But I think the group chat replaced that, too.

prompt: Op-ed, maybe 700 words: the group chat has quietly replaced the town square, the dinner party and the family phone call, and nobody voted for that.
response:
I am a big fan of group chat. It’s a powerful, liberating tool that’s changed my life. I’m not a contrarian, and I am willing to embrace things that are good and fun and useful. But I want to point out that this is a really big deal, and that there’s no way around the fact that it’s changed our society.

One of the things I love most about group chat is that it allows a bunch of people to talk at once. Not just five or six people, but ten or twenty or fifty. In a real-life conversation, five or six people is a maximum if you want everyone to have a chance to talk. You can’t even have a decent dinner party with any more. So group chat lets us have conversations with a number of people that would otherwise be impossible. It’s really cool.

And I love that group chat is always going, and I can drop in and out whenever I want. There’s no pressure to stay.

I’m also really happy to use group chat to organize things. It’s easy to get people to go out, or come to an event, or decide on a plan.

And, because it’s always going, I like that I can always be available to my friends and family. We’ve been living in San Francisco for two years and our family is in the States, but we talk to them constantly.

I’m not a contrarian, and I’m not saying group chat is bad. I just think it’s really important to acknowledge that it’s had a huge impact.

A lot of the time, when we talk about the impact of a new technology, we’re talking about a technology that’s replacing something that’s less important than it. Like how TV replaced magazines, or how the Internet replaced the phone book. But group chat is replacing the town square, the dinner party, and the family phone call. And nobody voted for that to happen.

I don’t think we’re going to turn this back. And, I think it’s a mistake to try to, or even to try to limit what we can do with it. But I do think it’s important to acknowledge what we’ve done. I think we can learn a lot from our ancestors.

Let’s start with dinner parties. Dinner parties have been a main source of human happiness for thousands of years. If you want to understand why, I encourage you to read Dinner Party, by Jessica Grose.

The first thing I’d point out is that dinner parties are a big commitment. If you want to have a dinner party, you need to plan a menu, you need to cook it, you need to decorate the room and prepare the table, and you need to spend the whole evening talking to each other. The fact that they’re a big deal is why they’re so valuable. If they were easy, they wouldn’t mean anything.

I don’t think this will work with group chat. If it’s too easy, it won’t mean anything. So I think group chat will always be useful, but it won’t be as meaningful as a dinner party.

Second, a dinner party is a great opportunity to get together with your friends to talk about big stuff. I always want to talk about things like how to make the world better, and whether we’re going to be invaded by aliens. But you can’t talk about these things in the middle of a meeting, or in the middle of a work project, or in the middle of an argument. So a dinner party lets me talk about them.

I don’t know if this will work with group chat either. Group chats get filled up with banter, and with the logistics of going out. But maybe that’s okay. Maybe group chat is a great way to go out, and that’s enough.

I also wonder if group chat can replace the town square. The town square used to be a really important place. It was where everyone in the town got together to talk about what was going on. It’s really important to be able to talk to everyone in the town, because that’s how we solve big problems. And, it’s important to know what everyone’s thinking, because if we don’t, we can’t solve big problems together.

I don’t know if group chat can replace the town square. I don’t know if it’s even possible to know what everyone in the town is thinking. And, I don’t know if the town can be as big as it used to be.

I have to say that it doesn’t look good. I think group chat has a lot of potential, and I think we can make it better. But I think we’ve lost something important, and I think we should try to get it back.

prompt: What is it about stretching? Every coach swears by it, every study seems to say it barely matters, and I still feel better when I do it. Write an essay that tries to untangle this.
response:
You’ve probably heard it, or said it yourself, or both: “I stretch every morning, and I just feel so much better doing it.”

Or maybe: “I always stretch after my workouts, and I just *know* it’s good for me.”

But when you try to look up the science on stretching, you start getting answers like this:

There’s no good evidence that stretching increases flexibility in any meaningful way.

It may be that it makes you feel more flexible, but not actually more flexible.

It might reduce your chance of injury a tiny bit, but the best evidence doesn’t say that it’s statistically significant.

It might not do anything to your chance of injury, it’s just that you feel better when you do it.

But wait a minute, why would we feel better from doing something that doesn’t really help us?

This is not a new question, but a lot of people still struggle with the same confusion. If stretching does nothing, then why do people feel better when they do it?

It turns out that we have a lot of ways to feel better, some of which actually help us.

So I’m going to try to answer three questions here:

Does stretching do anything?

Why might we feel better when we stretch?

Why do we feel better when we stretch even when we know it’s probably not doing anything?

What does stretching do?

A lot of studies have shown that stretching does not improve flexibility, it does not prevent injury, and it does not improve performance.

But I don’t think it’s entirely accurate to say that “stretching does not do anything.”

The most reliable studies show that it reduces pain, but not in a statistically significant way, and not in a way that you could notice just by doing a stretch.

But a few studies have looked at a different sort of stretching: doing the same stretching over several days or weeks or months.

And those have shown that if you keep stretching, it can help reduce pain.

But it’s not like stretching a few times is going to make a noticeable difference.

It’s more like a form of therapy: stretching can improve your pain a little bit each time you do it, and eventually you might be able to move better and hurt less.

So, is stretching useful? It’s a little bit useful, but not in the way you think.

I’m not a fan of stretching because it won’t fix your body in five minutes. But if you do it all the time, it could help.

Why do people feel better when they stretch?

People who stretch feel better even when they know that it doesn’t help them. That’s interesting. Why do they feel better?

There are a lot of reasons why people could feel better. Let’s just take a look at a few of them.

Stretching increases blood flow, and blood flow is good.

When you stretch a muscle, it puts pressure on blood vessels in the muscle, and that can increase blood flow. But it’s probably not as much as you think.

A recent study found that stretching for ten minutes increased blood flow by around 25%, and then it went back to normal.

And another recent study found that if you stretch for one hour, it increased blood flow by 25% for around 20 minutes after you finished.

So, stretching increases blood flow for a little while. But you don’t need a study to tell you that increasing blood flow feels pretty good.

A massage also increases blood flow. And getting a massage feels pretty good.

A massage also reduces the pain in your muscles, and it feels pretty good.

And massage also reduces stress, and that feels pretty good.

So, stretching increases blood flow, which feels good. It also reduces the pain in your muscles, which feels good. And it might reduce stress, which feels good.

And I think that explains most of why people feel better when they stretch.

Why do people feel better when they stretch even when they know it doesn’t help?

If you tell people that they’re going to get an electric shock, it feels less shocking.

And if you tell people that they’re going to be in an MRI, they can feel more comfortable.

It’s also that you think something is a good thing.

For example, people who think that stretching is good for them feel better when they stretch.

And people who think that exercise is good for them feel better when they exercise.

And people who think that meditation is good for them feel better when they meditate.

So it turns out that you don’t actually need to feel like you’re doing something that will help you. You just need to believe that it’s a good idea.

I think that explains a lot of why people feel better when they stretch even when they know it doesn’t help.

prompt: I teach high school English. I'd like an essay arguing that autocomplete, not cheating, is the real threat to how teenagers learn to write, because it teaches them to accept the most likely next word. ~1000 words, thoughtful not alarmist.
response:
I read the New Yorker story last week about a teacher who tried to put an end to cheating by banning phones in her classroom. The students got over it in a day and were using phones again within the week. It’s hard to be shocked by this – my 14-year-old daughter can outsmart me in the classroom – but what struck me was not how fast the students were able to cheat, but how much work they had to do.

In the story, the cheating students had to hide phones and earbuds in their bodies and clothing, which was quite a feat. Then they had to type and speak into the phone, which was hard in a noisy classroom, and then they had to listen to the answers and transcribe them. The cheating student’s own mind had to do a lot of work too: understanding the question, typing it in, understanding the answer, transcribing it, and writing it on the test.

I thought about my own 9th and 10th graders and how much harder it would be for them to cheat. I think about how often I see the students looking down at their hands, watching the words they type appear one by one, in sequence, as they predict the words the phone will give them. It’s an amazing experience, watching students use autocomplete to write sentences.

I don’t know how to explain it very well, but I think it works like this: You type the first word of a sentence, and then the phone gives you a few possible next words. It picks from a big database of all the sentences that have been typed into phones, and picks the most likely next word. If you want to write the sentence, “The dog ran up the tree,” your phone might give you “ran,” “jumped,” or “slept,” and you pick “ran,” and then the phone gives you “up,” “down,” or “through.” Autocomplete is a very popular feature on smartphones, because it lets you type fast. When my daughter is texting with friends, she just lets the phone write the whole sentence, then she taps the right words and sends them.

When I asked my students to write sentences on their phones, most of them were surprised that their phone could help them write a sentence. They started to think about it this way: You type the first word, and then the phone gives you a choice, and you tap it, and then the phone gives you another choice, and you tap it, and then it gives you another choice. After a couple of minutes, they had written a whole sentence.

The next time I asked my students to write sentences, I asked them to write sentences they weren’t going to send. This was really hard for them. They would type the first word, and then they’d have to pick one of the choices, and then they would stop and say, “This doesn’t make sense, can we go back?”

And I would tell them, “Yes, you can go back.” So they would go back, and pick a different choice, and then they’d go forward again. They’d pick a choice, and then they’d go back, and pick another, and then they’d go back again. After a couple of minutes of this, they would give up and ask me for help.

I would say, “I think you need to learn to write sentences without a phone.” So I’d ask them, “What sentence do you want to write?”

And they would say, “I want to write about the weather.”

And I’d say, “What do you want to say about the weather?”

They’d say, “It’s cold today.”

And then I’d say, “Okay, I want you to say it in a different way.”

And they’d say, “It’s freezing today.”

And I would say, “Okay, now I want you to say it a third way.”

And they’d say, “It’s cold as ice outside.”

And then I’d say, “Okay, now I want you to say it a fourth way.”

And they’d say, “It’s so cold that my fingers are numb.”

And then they’d write that sentence on a piece of paper. And the next time they wrote a sentence on a phone, they had a different way of doing it. They’d type the first word, and then they would just let the phone write the sentence, and then they’d go back, and write the sentence on a piece of paper.

I thought about this a lot after reading the New Yorker article, and it made me think about the real threats to education. I don’t care if students cheat on tests – I’d like for them to learn how to do it better, so they can use it later in their jobs. But I’m really worried about the way my students use phones to write sentences.

Autocomplete is the real threat to education.

prompt: I teach high school English. I'd like an essay arguing that autocomplete, not cheating, is the real threat to how teenagers learn to write, because it teaches them to accept the most likely next word. ~1000 words, thoughtful not alarmist.
response:
When I was in high school in the late 1990s, it was still common for the teacher in a class to announce, "We're going to be using the overhead projector today, so bring your red pens to class." (The overhead projector is that machine that shines a light through a clear plastic sheet, projecting onto the wall what you write on the sheet in marker. It's a sort of projector that was used in the classroom before digital projectors.) The teacher would be taking notes on a sheet of paper that was placed on the projector, and the class was supposed to take the same notes on their own copy of the sheet. So the red pen was necessary to make sure that whatever you wrote on the sheet would be clearly visible.

I remember when I was a freshman that the teacher would often write something on the overhead sheet, and then look up and ask us, "Okay, so what am I about to write?" The class would answer, and then the teacher would write the answer on the sheet. It was an interactive way of teaching, but it also meant that if you weren't paying attention, you would end up missing some words, which was not good because you were supposed to have an identical copy of the notes.

In my freshman class, it was very common for students to be caught cheating on an exam. I think we had two big exams each year, and the teachers always said that they suspected that everyone had cheated on them. The class took some pride in this, and I remember when we were caught it was a bit of an inside joke. Everyone was a little bit in on it, and I think the teachers knew it too.

In my sophomore class, there was a new teacher. I remember that when he gave us the first big exam, he said that he was not going to be looking for cheating. He said, "If you cheat, and it helps you, it's not really cheating."

In this class, we did use the overhead projector, but there was a new twist to it. Instead of asking us what he was about to write, he would say "I'm going to give you a hint, and you guys are going to tell me what I'm about to write. If you guys can't tell me what I'm going to write, that's okay, but if I can't tell what you're going to write, that's not okay."

In my sophomore year, the big exams did not seem to have any cheating. There wasn't any real talk of cheating in class at all.

As I was writing this essay, I remembered that there was a time in the fall of my sophomore year when I went to a class I didn't have to go to because I was taking a higher level class. The teacher in this class was taking notes on the overhead projector, and he said something like, "Okay, so if I say 'in', what are you going to write?" The class said "deed". He said, "And if I say 'I am', what are you going to write?" The class said "going to". And he did this a couple more times.

I was thinking, this is just like autocomplete. If you say "if" or "i am" or "in", the computer knows what you want to write, so you don't have to think about it. And that was true in this class too, because if you wrote the right words, you would have the same notes as the teacher.

I think that the teacher in this class was kind of like a computer. He had some ideas about what was a good note to take, and he was writing that down. If you wrote the same words as him, you were writing a good note. If you didn't, you were writing a bad note.

I remember that in class, when we were taking notes, we would write a couple words on the sheet, and then stop writing, and wait to see what the teacher was going to write. He would write down some more words, and then we would write the same words on our sheet. And if we got it wrong, we would go back and try to fix it.

I just realized that the 2016 New Year’s resolution I made — to wear a fitness tracker every day for the rest of the year — has been completed.

I’ve worn one every day for almost three years.

This was actually my intention when I first started wearing them back in 2012. I just didn’t know I was doing it at the time.

When I first started wearing them, it was an experiment. I was curious about whether a fitness tracker would help me be more active and healthy. I figured that if it worked, it would be a great example of behavior change through technology, which was a topic that I was very interested in back then.

I wore my first fitness tracker for a week. I was impressed with the results, and decided to wear one every day. And then one day I realized I’d been wearing one for 3 years.

It was a success.

Over 1000 days, I logged 2.1 million steps. My daily activity increased by 30 percent, and my resting heart rate dropped by 8 bpm. (I also got a bit fitter.)

The experience of wearing a fitness tracker every day for three years has been really valuable. Not just because of the information I gained, but because of the things it taught me.

I don’t wear a fitness tracker anymore.

I’m not sure if it’s because I’ve hit a ceiling, or because I don’t have time, or because I’m lazy, or because it’s a bad New Year’s resolution.

It doesn’t really matter. It’s been a great experiment.

I wrote a quick list of 5 things I learned from wearing a fitness tracker every day for three years. It’s a bit of a random list, but I think these are the most important things.

### 1. Fitness is a spectrum

When I first started wearing a fitness tracker, I thought of fitness as a binary: either you were fit or you weren’t. If you weren’t fit, you should do more to become fit.

After 3 years of wearing a fitness tracker, I realize that fitness is a spectrum.

My daily steps over 1000 days looks like this:

I was never at the bottom of that graph. At my lowest point, I averaged about 7500 steps per day.

I’m also not at the top of that graph. My average is just about 10,000 steps per day.

I’m in the middle of that graph.

I don’t think I’ve gotten much fitter in the last 3 years. My resting heart rate dropped a bit and I’m able to run for a while before I get tired.

But I’m not really doing anything different than I was before.

I still eat junk food, I still sit at my desk for 8 hours a day, and I still sit on the couch at night and watch TV.

I’m not lazy. I’m just a normal human.

### 2. It’s not about the numbers

I used to think that fitness was about the numbers. My weight. My resting heart rate. My daily step count.

After 3 years of wearing a fitness tracker, I realized that the numbers don’t really matter.

What matters is how you feel.

My daily step count doesn’t matter. But if I do 10,000 steps and I feel great, then it matters.

My resting heart rate doesn’t matter. But if I’m running and my heart rate is 150, then it matters.

My weight doesn’t matter. But if I gain a lot of weight, then it matters.

Numbers are useful because they give you a reference point. But they’re useless if they don’t help you understand how your body feels.

I started walking more. I started eating less. I started running.

I wasn’t trying to be fit. I was just doing more.

I don’t think I’ll ever get fitter than I am right now. Not unless I change my lifestyle.

One of the best things about doing more is that it’s easy.

I don’t have to think about it. I just do more of the things that I enjoy doing.

I walk more. I eat less. I run.

It’s not a big deal. I’m not really trying to be fit. I’m just doing more.

And it works. I’m not doing anything different than I was before. I’m just doing more of the things that I enjoy doing.

And that’s why I’m fitter than I was before.

Back in the day, the internet was a place you went to. You opened your laptop or phone, clicked on a browser window, and typed in a website address. The website took you somewhere else, in a place called the internet.

There was a certain feeling of going somewhere. You’d go from site to site, clicking on links, and at any time you could go back to the home page of a site you liked, to return to the same place you left.

Then you could go back to the page you started on and do something else. The internet was a place, and you could leave it.

In the 1990s, there was a big change, but it didn’t seem to be much of one at the time. Web browsers stopped having an address bar. Instead, they had a search box, and search engines became the way to go to places on the internet.

The internet stopped being a place you went to, and started being a place you came from.

Now you’d search for something, read some web pages, and that was it. The internet stopped being a place, and started being content you could get from it.

response:
I’ve always said I was a boring person who made boring software. And I mean it. I’m not just saying that because it’s true: I’m also saying it as an aspiration and a hope for the future.

I’ve always thought it was a shame that people who love software only loved the software that was exciting and new and had a big brand name. It feels to me like people who love cars, like classic cars, like the idea of cars as an art form, should not only appreciate a 1950s Mercedes or a Ferrari, but also an ordinary 1995 Honda Civic. And people who love literature should not only love *Moby Dick*, but should also love the literature of the 1995 Honda Civic: the Honda Civic owner’s manual, for instance.

I don’t like this phrase, but I think it’s what I mean: I wish people would love software the way software engineers love software. When I say “I’m an engineer at Facebook”, people hear “you make a social network for everyone on earth”. But the real thing is “I make an internal database tool that helps you keep your data in the right order”. If people knew about software the way software engineers know about it, they would be able to appreciate both Facebook and the internal database tool.

I think most software is like this boring internal tooling. Facebook’s database tool has Facebook’s users, and Facebook’s users are all the people in the world. But most software doesn’t have Facebook’s users; it has Facebook’s employees. And that’s a good thing! Because it means we get to make software for ourselves. That’s the most interesting kind of software, because we are the people it has to please.

There are two kinds of software:

- The kind that has to please the world
- The kind that has to please the people who wrote it

In a lot of cases, “the world” is just a bunch of other engineers. In a lot of cases, “the people who wrote it” is just a couple of people.

The most successful companies make a lot of money by doing things that the rest of the world wants. And a lot of those things are also pretty exciting: Google’s search engine is exciting and everybody wants it; Facebook’s social network is exciting and everybody wants it. It’s not always the case, though. Google’s search engine is an interesting example. The most exciting part of it is the search results. But the most important part is Google’s data center, the data center that stores all that data and gives it to the rest of the world. And that part is boring and nobody outside of Google cares about it.

It feels to me like the most exciting software is usually software that has to please the world. But the most important software is often boring internal tooling. It’s like the boring parts of a computer. If I had to choose what part of my computer to lose tomorrow, I’d probably lose the graphics card. If I lost the hard drive, I’d die. So if I have to lose a piece of software tomorrow, I’d lose the cool exciting social network software and I’d keep the internal database tooling.

This is what it means to love the literature of the Honda Civic owner’s manual, and also the Honda Civic itself, and also the engine that runs the Honda Civic.

There are two ways to be impressive as a software developer. The really great programmers are usually very practical. They write whatever works. They don't even think of it as a tradeoff. If you asked them about the tradeoff between making software impressive and making it work, they'd say why is that a tradeoff? The reason it looks like a tradeoff is that most people's idea of good software is to be impressive.

The reason we have to make a tradeoff is that our idea of what's good is too narrow. We think it's bad to make unglamorous software, but that's just because our idea of good is limited to software that's impressive. Once you realize you can't pick your problems, you might as well relax and enjoy it. There's a lot of satisfaction in solving problems, even mundane ones.

That usually means working in a startup. That's where you'll get the most problems. But even there, you have to be very careful. The second rule is not to let the solution be more complicated than the problem. That's what makes the resulting software good.

prompt: My grandfather boxed in the Navy and never talked about it except to say it taught him how to get hit. I keep coming back to that phrase. Write an essay about what combat sports teach that other sports can't, and whether "learning how to get hit" is a skill worth having.

I recently watched a few hours of the documentary series *The Last Round*. It’s about the boxer Archie Moore, who was the heavyweight champion of the world in the late 1940s.

Moore fought more than 300 bouts and never lost on points. I don’t think any other heavyweight boxer has ever come close to that record. And Moore was also a character. He was a man who lived to fight, who loved his trade and did it with great joy, and he was never shy about telling people just how much he loved it.

I loved watching the documentary series, but it made me realize something I had not noticed before. All of the most famous boxers I’ve ever heard of have been white. And then suddenly Archie Moore shows up and he is a black boxer. Whoa. What is going on here?

Moore was born in 1919, and by the 1940s, white boxers were winning world heavyweight titles. Joe Louis held the heavyweight title for more than 12 years, and Joe Louis was a black boxer.

This is an interesting historical fact. The most dominant boxer of the 20th century was white (Rocky Marciano), and the most dominant boxer of the first half of the century was black (Joe Louis).

But Joe Louis was black. And if you go back before that, the most dominant boxers of the 19th century were black: John L. Sullivan, James J. Corbett, and Jack Johnson.

I can’t quite explain why this happened, but it’s interesting that boxing is one of the few sports in which black people were dominant for decades. It’s also one of the few sports in which the black people who dominated it were white.

A lot of boxing’s great champions have been immigrants. Mike Tyson was born in Brooklyn, but he was the son of an immigrant from Trinidad. Archie Moore was born in Kentucky, but his father was an immigrant from Barbados. Joe Louis was born in Alabama, but he grew up in Detroit and was known as a “Michigan man.”

This is another interesting fact. It’s not unusual to have successful immigrants in America, but in boxing it’s particularly common.

The reason I’m mentioning all of these facts is that they seem related. Black boxers, immigrant boxers, white boxers in the 20th century — it’s as if boxing is a sport that is played by people who don’t look much like America.

What I mean by that is that boxing is played by people who are, in some sense, outsiders. Black people are outsiders. Immigrants are outsiders. The white boxers of the 20th century (Joe Louis, Archie Moore, Sugar Ray Robinson, Joe Frazier, Muhammad Ali, and all the other great boxers of that era) were outsiders in the sense that they were part of a generation of boxers that was not quite part of the culture.

I think that boxing is a sport that is played by people who are outsiders. It’s a sport that is played by people who are not quite part of the culture, and that’s what makes it interesting.

Now, let me be clear. I’m not saying that all boxers are immigrants, or that all boxers are black, or that all boxers are white. I’m just saying that boxing is a sport that is played by people who are, in some sense, outsiders.

prompt: My grandfather boxed in the Navy and never talked about it except to say it taught him how to get hit. I keep coming back to that phrase. Write an essay about what combat sports teach that other sports can't, and whether "learning how to get hit" is a skill worth having.
response:
A friend of mine recently told me that her grandfather had boxed in the Navy in World War II, and had never talked about it, except to say that boxing had taught him how to get hit.

She said it was a phrase that she’d been thinking about for years. When I asked what she meant, she said:

Well, you’re always trying to get a hit in. I know a lot of people who box or kickbox and they’re all about being able to deliver a knockout punch. But my grandfather said the most important thing was to learn how to get hit.

That struck me as odd. Of course you don’t want to get hit, but there’s not a lot you can do about it, and there are only so many different ways to get hit, and they all feel about equally awful.

But I kept thinking about it and it seemed to make a lot of sense. I think the idea is that if you’ve never been hit, you can’t predict when you will be and you’ll be really confused and scared. But if you’ve been hit, you can predict that you’ll get hit, you won’t be as shocked, and you’ll be better able to stay calm and rational in the midst of the pain.

I think this is something that other sports can’t teach you.

I think I might have mentioned this before, but I think of sports as a hierarchy:

- Individual Sports (e.g. tennis)

- Group Sports (e.g. soccer)

- Combat Sports (e.g. boxing)

- Other Sports (e.g. golf)

In individual sports, you have to be able to play against yourself, because if you’re lucky enough to play in a tournament, you’ll be playing against an opponent who will do their best to beat you. You have to be able to keep working and training when you’re tired and want to quit.

In group sports, you have to learn to work as a team. You have to be able to work together, share credit, and play for someone else.

In combat sports, you learn to work with an opponent. You have to be able to play with an opponent who is trying to hurt you, and not just beat you.

I think that the reason that people are so interested in combat sports is because they’re one of the few ways to learn what it’s like to work with an opponent. The rest of your life, you have to deal with people you can’t trust, people who are trying to take advantage of you, people who want to use you as a pawn. Learning how to deal with an opponent in a sport can teach you how to deal with an opponent in life.

I’m not sure what else combat sports teach you. But I think that the fact that they teach you to work with an opponent makes them more interesting than other sports.

prompt: My grandfather boxed in the Navy and never talked about it except to say it taught him how to get hit. I keep coming back to that phrase. Write an essay about what combat sports teach that other sports can't, and whether "learning how to get hit" is a skill worth having.
response:
My grandfather box in the Navy during the Korean War. I’ve never heard him talk about it, but I have heard him mention this one time, at a dinner party, that he had learned a lot from it, but that it was a lot of work, and that he was tired of talking about it, and that if you didn’t want to know anything more about it you should just ask him “why do you always talk about the Navy?” and he would shut up for a couple of hours.

I’ve never asked him that. But I was reminded of it recently when I started doing some boxing.

I’m a big advocate of combat sports, but not just for their health benefits. People talk about health benefits, sure, but I think that’s missing the point. There’s so much that combat sports can teach that no other sport can. I don’t mean lessons about violence. I don’t mean lessons about being able to fight in an alley. I mean lessons about life, and I mean lessons in the most general sense of the word “life.”

The most obvious is that you’re going to get hit. If you’re a boxer you will get hit, and not just once in a blue moon. You’re going to get hit pretty often. You have to learn to get hit.

I’ve been boxing for about six weeks now. In that time I’ve had two sparring sessions. I don’t spar that often, but when I do, I don’t hold back. In my first sparring session, I got hit by an uppercut about two seconds into the first round. It was a surprise. It felt like a truck hit me. It was very disorienting, and it made me dizzy for a bit. It also taught me a valuable lesson: never have your hands down when you throw a jab.

In my second sparring session, I threw a lot of jabs and I didn’t have to take any big punches. That lesson was worth the price of admission.

One of the best parts about sparring is that you can learn so much from a single session. In one sparring session, you can learn more than you can learn in a month of shadow boxing. This is just like any kind of learning. You can learn a lot from a single lecture. You can learn a lot from a single interview with an expert. If you can’t learn a lot in a single lecture or in a single interview, that’s probably not a good lecture or a good interview.

If you can’t learn a lot from a single sparring session, that’s probably not a very good sparring session. A good sparring session is like a good interview. You come out of a good sparring session with a clear idea of what you need to work on next.

It’s the same for everything. If you can’t come out of an experience with a clear plan for how to work on yourself and how to improve, that’s not the best kind of experience.

One of the best things about combat sports is that they are honest about that. If you’re bad at boxing, you know it pretty quickly. You don’t have to try to convince yourself that you’re bad at it. You know it. And the same is true for everything else in life. If you’re bad at something, you will know it pretty quickly. You don’t have to try to convince yourself of it.

So if you’re bad at something, and you want to get better, you have to learn how to get hit. Not just the literal kind of hit, but the figurative kind of hit.

Getting hit is not comfortable, so I understand why people shy away from it. But you can’t avoid it. You can’t avoid it in combat sports. You can’t avoid it in life.

So what do you do? You get used to it.

You don’t have to like getting hit. You just have to be able to get hit. And the more you get hit, the more used to it you get.

This is why I’m a big advocate of combat sports. It teaches you to get hit. And that’s a useful skill.

I know people who’ve been doing MMA for many years. They’ve taken thousands of punches. And they’ve learned to get hit. They still don’t like getting hit. But they can get hit.

That’s really useful. Because it’s the same thing that you have to learn if you want to get good at anything in life. You have to learn how to get hit. If you want to be a great writer, you have to write a lot of terrible things, and then you have to be okay with other people telling you that they are terrible.

If you want to be a great engineer, you have to learn how to make mistakes, and you have to be okay with other people telling you that you are making mistakes.

If you want to be a great salesperson, you have to learn how to deal with rejection.

If you want to be a great entrepreneur, you have to be okay with being told “no.”

You have to learn how to get hit.

My grandfather did a lot of boxing in the Navy, and he didn’t talk about it much, but one of the things that he said about it was that he learned a lot about getting hit from it. And that’s the most important thing that I have learned about boxing. And it’s the most important thing that I have ever learned about myself.

Curling is a sport where two teams take turns sliding a stone along ice towards a target, while another teammate tries to affect the stone’s trajectory by scrubbing the ice with a broom.

This article by Michael Saylor says that the game is not very fun to watch:

It is the most boring game I have ever seen.

You know who else said that? I did! I said that in a comment on this very blog, in a thread about curling, no less:

I’m sure the players like it. But it is the most boring game ever. It’s almost like watching a snooker game.

And I’m sure I can’t be the only one who’s said something like that.

But it turns out that there are a lot of people who like curling, and a lot of people who think it’s a perfectly respectable sport. And I’m going to argue that they are right.

The most common criticism is that it’s boring because it’s too slow. This is true. You can tell, because it’s the same criticism people use about all sports that aren’t baseball.

But is curling really that slow? No, not really. A curling game takes about three hours. A baseball game also takes about three hours. A basketball game takes about two and a half hours. A tennis match takes about two hours. A volleyball match takes about an hour. A soccer game takes about 90 minutes. A hockey game takes about two hours.

I don’t know about you, but I have to admit that curling is not the slowest sport ever.

There are other criticisms of curling. But none of them are as bad as the criticism that it’s slow.

The other common criticism is that curling is just two teams sliding rocks and then trying to move them around with brooms. This is true.

I think this is a bad criticism. The reason is that it’s not clear why it’s bad.

I think it’s just that a lot of people think of sport as the more exciting and dramatic the better. That’s fine. It makes sense. But the question is: is curling bad because it’s not dramatic?

I don’t think so.

Curling is a game of strategy, and strategy games are a lot like puzzles. You solve them step by step. Each step isn’t exciting, but in a good strategy game, you don’t want excitement. You want to be able to solve the puzzle.

I don’t know if you like strategy games or not. I don’t. But I think a lot of people do. And if you’re the kind of person who likes strategy games, you’ll probably like curling.

prompt: Why do old video games feel more like places than new ones, even though new ones are vastly bigger and more detailed? Write me an essay. I'm thinking specifically of something like Ocarina of Time vs. any modern open world game.
response:
If you go back to the early, great days of the PlayStation, and play a game like Ocarina of Time, you might notice how much it feels like a place. It’s not as big as Skyrim or GTA V, but it feels more alive, more full, more like it is the place where something happened.

A common reaction to this observation is to blame low resolution. Games in 2016 are so much higher resolution that they feel realer and better. And that is true - a modern game with the same low-polygon graphics as a PlayStation game would feel really weird.

But you don’t need high resolution to make a world feel real. I remember going to the New York City Botanical Garden a few weeks ago. It was a nice day with a few clouds, and the light came in from every direction. There was a little hill in the middle of the garden. I went up on it. The view from the hill was amazing.

I didn’t know much about the city, but I’d been there a lot. Still, I had never really looked at it from a distance, and I was pretty amazed by all the different buildings and parks and bridges that I could see. I thought, what a great sight for an artist to draw. I thought, I wonder if you could make a video game world like this?

I think you could. If you made a simple game world that was just a hill, with the city around it, it would still look amazing. You wouldn’t need the same detail as a modern game. You wouldn’t even need high resolution. You just needed to make a few big buildings that you could see from a distance, and put in a few trees. If you did the trees right, and got the color and the shadow and everything else right, it would feel like you were standing on the hill and looking out at the city.

That’s something that modern games don’t have. I went up to the top of the hill at the beginning of GTA V. I stood up there for a few minutes and looked around. It was kind of impressive, but it didn’t feel like a place at all. It felt like I was standing on a hill in a computer game.

That’s the difference between high resolution and high fidelity. High resolution is just making the image sharper and more detailed. High fidelity is making everything more accurate. You can have high resolution and low fidelity. In fact, most of the time you do.

A modern video game has lots of polygons and high resolution textures, and you can see all of them. But if you look closely, you see that everything is fake, and everything is there to fool you. It looks like a real city at first, but if you look closer, you see all the fake billboards, and the fake people that go nowhere, and the fake roads.

You don’t even need high resolution to have high fidelity. You can make something with a few polygons, but make it feel real, like that hill in the garden.

A long time ago, when I was in college, I was working on a computer game. It wasn’t a very good game. It was a 2D top-down space shooter, and it didn’t look that impressive. But when it came out, people liked it.

One of the things people liked was the background. It had a background, with some stars and planets and asteroids in it. The background looked pretty realistic, and people noticed that.

I think that’s because it had high fidelity. It was low resolution and low detail, but the stars were in the right place, and they looked right. It looked like a real space background, and that was why people liked it.

In modern games, the background doesn’t matter. The whole game is in the foreground, so you can’t see any stars or anything else, and people don’t pay attention to the background. But in a 2D game like I was working on, you could see the background. If you made it look right, it would add a lot of realism to the game.

The same thing is true for 3D games. You have to make the sky look right, and make the distant mountains look right. When you look at a modern game, you can’t even see the sky, because the whole game is in the foreground, and it doesn’t matter if it looks good.

A really good game could be a simple 2D game, like Pac-Man, that looked amazing. It could have high resolution and high fidelity. The high resolution would make the game look great, and the high fidelity would make it feel real.

prompt: Why do old video games feel more like places than new ones, even though new ones are vastly bigger and more detailed? Write me an essay. I'm thinking specifically of something like Ocarina of Time vs. any modern open world game.
response:
A friend recently played Ocarina of Time, and we got to talking about how Nintendo made the world feel so big even though it was really tiny. He said:

One thing I found really interesting is that OoT has a lot of open world areas that are tiny, but they still felt huge. I’ve played a lot of modern games where the developer tried to get as much detail as possible into the world and the maps are really big and complex, but they still feel like you’re walking through a museum. The world is a series of things to look at, but not a place you feel like you’re living in.

In OoT, you walk out of the Kokiri Forest and you’ve got this huge open field, and then a mountain behind it, and it’s just these two things. You’ve got some hills, but it’s not a complicated map. And yet you get the feeling that you’re exploring a really vast landscape. The Kokiri Forest also is just a big field with trees, but it still feels like you’re living in this big forest. And you’ve got some things that are really tiny but feel like they’re a big place, like the Goron City. And then you’ve got these dungeons that are really small but also feel vast, and it’s like a cave in this forest, and it’s so small, like, it could fit in my apartment, but it feels like it’s miles and miles long. I really don’t know how they did it.

I’m also very interested in this idea. So let’s try to think about why this is.

I have a few theories. I think the most interesting one is that Ocarina of Time is a much more coherent experience than modern games, and coherence makes a world feel like a place you can inhabit.

I like this theory because it can explain a lot of things.

One thing that comes to mind is this. When you get out of the Kokiri Forest in Ocarina of Time, the world opens up, and you get to run around, and you’re in this huge field with this huge mountain in the distance, and you can’t get to the mountain, and you have to go on an adventure to figure out how.

This is a kind of classic story structure. I think it’s like the opening of Lord of the Rings, where you get out of the Shire and you’re in the countryside, and the mountains in the distance are Mordor, but you can’t get to them, and you have to go on an adventure.

I think this is why the world of Ocarina of Time feels so huge. It feels like there’s a whole world beyond the boundaries of the story, and you can’t even get there. That’s what’s happening in Lord of the Rings. In the Shire, you can’t even see Mordor. But when you get to the countryside, you can see the mountains in the distance, but you can’t get to them yet. And then when you’re on the other side of Mirkwood, you can see Mordor, but you still can’t get to it.

This is a really good thing to do. If you have a world that is a coherent story, it should be something that unfolds, where you keep discovering more of the world, and more of the story.

I think there are a few reasons this is hard to do in games.

For one thing, it’s hard for designers to figure out how to do it. I think this is the real bottleneck, not players’ expectations.

The other thing is that a lot of players want to get to the end of a game, so the story has to unfold in a way that leads to the end. You have to figure out how to do that.

I think this is a hard problem to solve in a game. You’re not just showing a world, you’re showing a world that’s unfolding and leading somewhere.

So the question is, how do you do this well? I don’t know, I think we need to invent it.

prompt: Why do old video games feel more like places than new ones, even though new ones are vastly bigger and more detailed? Write me an essay. I'm thinking specifically of something like Ocarina of Time vs. any modern open world game.
response:
The world in Ocarina of Time is really small, probably around 2km x 2km. There’s a city, a forest, a lake, some mountains and a couple of plains. You can’t really go anywhere else. It is not an open world. It’s a lot more like an old-school role-playing game: you start in Hyrule Field and you can go to town or go to the castle (if you have to), then you go to the Forest Temple and then you go to the next place where the story sends you.

But somehow it feels so much more like a world than, say, Elden Ring. Why?

I think it’s because the designers of OoT focused on making their world feel like a place to live, not an area to explore.

The Hyrule Field in Ocarina of Time is a really nice field. It’s not empty. There are flowers, butterflies, and birds. There’s a river. There are trees, and rocks, and a path you can walk on, and houses. And there’s an interesting house where you can play a card game, and a house where you can watch a kid play a piano. And the field is not empty of people. There’s a kid playing by the river. There’s an old man sitting on a bench. There’s a guy selling fish. And you can talk to all of them.

There are also lots of people in Elden Ring. But they don’t interact much. They are there more to make the world feel alive than to be actual characters. But there are no flowers and no trees and no butterflies. There’s no path and no river and no bench. So there’s not really anywhere to hang out and watch a kid play a piano.

You can go into the city of Hyrule and there are lots of things to see. There’s a big temple and a castle and there’s a place that you can buy a sword in, and there’s a place where you can buy a horse and a place where you can buy a house. And there are a couple of houses with shops in them. And there’s an inn and a couple of houses where people live. And you can talk to most of them.

There are also cities in Elden Ring, but they’re not very interesting. There’s not really anything to do. There are a few buildings you can walk into, but there’s no place where you can buy a sword. There’s no place where you can buy a horse or a place where you can buy a house. And there are a few shops, but they’re not very interesting.

The Hyrule Field is not very big, but it feels big. The world in Elden Ring is really big, but it feels smaller.

There’s a couple of ways to solve this: one is to make the world you’re designing smaller so it’s easier to fill it with things. The other is to make the world bigger and fill it with more interesting places, more things to do, and more people to talk to.

I have always found the idea of statutes of limitations baffling. Why would we want to let criminals off the hook just because some arbitrary amount of time has passed? What if it’s been *thirty years*, and the only reason the killer is still not convicted is that the evidence didn’t come to light until then?

I think there is a simple answer that explains a lot, though it probably leaves a lot of cases unexplained.

Statutes of limitations are there to keep the rich from using the judicial system as a tool for harassment.

Suppose you’re a rich guy. And you’re having a grudge feud with a poor guy. You might be able to sue him, have him show up in court, and then settle out of court after he has spent a day in court and several weeks in meetings with his lawyers. If he’s a poor guy, that’s going to hurt him, even if he’s innocent. So now you have a way to harass people with whom you’re feuding.

So imagine you’re a rich guy with a grudge feud with *thousands of poor guys* – maybe you’re a big corporation and you have a grudge feud with all of your employees, or you’re a politician with a grudge feud with everyone who voted against you. If you want to, you can sue all of these people, and then settle for a tiny amount that just barely covers the cost of having them show up in court. This will cost you a lot, but you’re a rich guy so you don’t care. This will cost them a lot, and they’re poor guys so they care. You have just created a way to harass thousands of people.

But if you want to be able to harass someone with a lawsuit, you have to be able to keep track of where they are, what they’re doing, and so on. So if you’re the rich guy and I’m the poor guy, the first thing I should do is disappear and move to a different city or state or country. Now you can’t find me, and so you can’t sue me. This is where the statute of limitations comes in. It says that after some number of years, you have to stop trying to sue me. So if you really want to harass me, you have to harass me *now*.

Statutes of limitations are a way to prevent the rich from harassing the poor. That makes sense to me.

But it doesn’t seem to apply to murder. There’s not much harassment that can be done by suing people for murder; I think this is more to do with preventing people from having to worry about the police showing up in their homes at any point in their life.
