response:
When I was 17, I was pretty sure the most important thing I was going to do in life was win the Nobel Prize in physics. I wasn’t crazy to think so. Plenty of other people had thought so at the same age, and gone on to do it.

The most famous example is Einstein, who was only 25 when he published his paper on special relativity. But Einstein was an outlier in that he was working outside the normal channels. Among people going through the usual route to win Nobel prizes — get a PhD, then work as a researcher — 25 was also the median age for those who won prizes for work they did in their 20s. There were plenty of precedents for the 17 year old who wanted to get a PhD by 25, then win a Nobel Prize shortly afterward.

In fact, a lot of people my age wanted to win Nobel prizes. The idea was so widespread that we had a name for it. It was called “doing something great.”

I can’t remember exactly when I stopped thinking I might do something great. It was definitely before college. I didn’t want to be a physicist anymore by then. But I must have stopped thinking I might do something great in any field when I stopped thinking of myself as being in the top 1% of my peers in terms of intelligence. You had to be that good to be on track to win a Nobel Prize.

The realization that I wouldn’t do something great was depressing, but I could afford to be depressed about it. There were so many other things I could do. I could still do something good, at least. And if I had to choose between something great and something good, I’d always choose something good.

What I didn’t realize then, or for a long time after, was how important it would be to me to keep thinking I might do something great. That I’d spend the next 15 years, unconsciously, trying to get myself back into a position where it could happen.

Now that I’m 52, it’s a bit too late for me to do something great. I think I peaked 5 years ago. Nothing bad happened to make me stop getting better, I just know I’m not going to get better. I can see the curve, and I know where it flattens out.

I’m not sad about it. If anything, it makes me more confident. The idea that I might be getting better is a good one to have, but it comes at the cost of a nagging doubt that you might already be at your peak. When you’re 40 and you know you’re already as good as you’re going to be, it’s reassuring to be able to say “that’s how good I am.”

And if anything, being 52 gives me more confidence about what I’ll be doing 10 years from now. The people I was worried about when I was 25 were the people who were 10 years younger. But I’m 52 now, so I can see what they did — which was nothing particularly impressive. And I know what the people 10 years younger than me now are going to do, too. It’s not much.

When I was 25, there was a famous physicist 10 years younger than me who seemed more promising than I was. When I was 35, there was a famous mathematician 10 years younger than me who seemed more promising than I was. And it seemed to me there had to be someone just as promising as me who was 10 years younger than me — indeed, I myself, 10 years earlier. When I was 45, I realized I was wrong about that last assumption. There wasn’t. And that means there’s no one now who is just as promising as me and 10 years younger than me.

When I was 35, there were people 10 years younger than me who seemed more promising than I was, but who in fact would turn out to be less impressive. I can tell because now, 10 years later, I can see how their careers have panned out. There was no one who seemed more promising than me but whose career turned out to be as impressive as mine. And there are no one who seem more promising than me and whose careers will be as impressive as mine.

If you’ve ever wondered why people seem more impressive when they’re young, this is one reason. They’re not just less impressive in the sense of having accomplished less. They’re also less impressive than you think.

Now that I know my peak, it feels good to have it behind me. But it also raises some questions. What do I do now? How do I use my remaining ambition?

The way to describe the next 15 years is that I’m going to keep doing what I’ve been doing. Which is not really an answer.

The answer to “what do I do now?” is “the same thing I do now.” That was the answer all along. I didn’t have to ask this question. It wasn’t necessary to make a decision at this point. I didn’t have to stop doing the work I was doing and start something new.

I’m not saying it will be obvious to everyone when it’s their turn to answer this question. It may not be. But for me it is obvious. What I’m going to do next is work, like I’ve been doing. And when people ask me what that will be like, I say “what it is now.”

But it’s not just the fact that I’ll still be working. That’s the obvious part. The important part is what I’ll be working on. And the answer is — what I’m working on now. The thing I was doing last year and the thing I was doing 5 years ago.

I’m still working on the same thing I was when I graduated college, 26 years ago. I know the answer, now, because I looked and see if that’s true.

I was working on computers. I was still working on computers. I’m still working on computers.

What about 10 years from now? I’ll still be working on computers. And 10 years after that. I’m not sure when I’ll stop working on computers. Probably never.

I’m not even sure when I’ll stop working on Y Combinator. That seems like a more reasonable question. But the only reason to think I will is that I’m getting old. But that seems like an arbitrary reason to stop working on something. I know that I’ll be working on something. Why not this thing?

This seems a bit of a cheat, though. The answer to “what do I do now?” shouldn’t be “what I’ve been doing” if the reason I was working on it was because it was the best way to make the thing I was doing next.

That does seem like the right answer, though. You don’t work on one thing as a way to get to the next. You work on one thing because you’re working on it. If the reason you’re working on X is to get to Y, you shouldn’t be working on X.

This doesn’t seem to apply in this case, though. It’s not that I’m working on computers because they’re the best way to get to Y Combinator. I just happen to be working on both right now. I’ll keep working on both. And if you think that’s not a real answer, that I’m just avoiding the question by saying I’m going to do what I’ve been doing, well, that’s what I’m going to do.

I’m not sure why people are so afraid of doing what they’ve been doing. It seems like a perfectly good answer.

prompt: Argue against 'follow your passion' - but not the usual way (it's bad career advice). Argue that passion is a bad guide to how to live at all.
response:
It’s been suggested recently that my “Do what you love” article was too narrow, that the best career advice was “live a life you’re proud of.” So you should choose a career that’s not just fun to do, but that you won’t be ashamed of when you tell people about it.

I agree, but I worry that “live a life you’re proud of” might be the wrong advice for the same reason. “Proud” is a word that implies a standard. If you’re proud of something, you feel it measures up to some standard you’re trying to meet.

If you try to live a life that measures up to some standard, you will inevitably make a living, not a life, out of that standard. I don’t believe this is the best way to live. It’s a trap.

There’s an old saying that the best way to live is to follow your heart. It’s often presented as career advice, but it’s really advice about life in general. The problem is, it’s not advice either. It’s a warning.

A lot of people follow their hearts. Unfortunately, they’re usually following the wrong ones. If you have a heart, you have a lot of hearts. We all have one that’s the organ that pumps blood around. And we all have an “inner voice” that’s like a conscience or a sense of what’s right. That’s probably what they mean by “heart” when they tell you to follow it. But we also have a heart that’s the seat of our desires. And that one tends to be wrong about what you want. It’s not a good guide, even to what you want, let alone what’s right.

The reason is that what you want is not a fixed thing. It changes as you change. But when you follow your heart, the heart you start with is the wrong one. Your heart has to change in order to learn what you really want. If you listen to it too literally, you’ll end up with a heart that’s been shaped by your own desires.

The best way to live is not to follow your heart but to change your heart.

The trouble with the inner voice is that it’s not always very loud. If you’re in a noisy place, you’re not going to hear it. But there’s an even more serious problem. The inner voice is not always right. It’s only an approximation of what’s right. What’s right, by definition, is what the right inner voice would tell you. So it’s not enough to listen to your inner voice. You have to improve it, and the way to do that is by changing your heart.

One of the things that distinguishes great minds from ordinary ones is that they know how to change their hearts. They’re not just clever. They’re not just fast. They change their minds. Not just about particular things. They change their minds about things in general. If there’s a better way to think about things, they’re always open to it. And because they’re open to new ideas, their ideas are always changing.

The most extreme example of changing one’s heart was probably Jesus, whose whole point was that the Old Testament was wrong, and he was going to fix it. It’s hard to do this without making a lot of enemies, but he did it anyway.

And so are all great people. They change the world by changing their own hearts. And the only way to do that is to be open to change.

It’s a lot less obvious than it sounds to be open to change.

If you want to be open to change, the first thing you have to be open to is change. Most people don’t want to change, even when they’re open to the idea of change. It’s not enough to say, as the Buddhists do, that change is the essence of life. You have to go one step further and say, as they do not, that change is the source of life. That change is what gives life meaning.

It’s very hard to accept this. I think it’s hard partly because we have so little time. We have such a short time to learn what we’re really about that any change seems a threat. That may be why our default is to be open only to certain kinds of change. If you tell people they have to change, they usually understand it to mean change in a bad way. If you tell them they’re supposed to change, you might as well have told them they’re supposed to get worse.

The default, though, is not to change. The change that most people want is the kind that doesn’t really affect their lives very much. If you tell them they have to change, they think you mean change like that.

If you have to change a lot in a short time, you can’t do it all by yourself. The only way to change quickly is to let other people change you. Which is the second thing you have to be open to: influence.

There’s one more thing you have to be open to. That’s the fact that influence is not a good thing in itself. It can be a good or a bad thing.

You can change a lot by being open to influence, but if you’re open to anything, you’ll be changed by everything. Which means you’ll be changed by bad things as well as good. The way to make sure you’re only changed by good things is to be open only to good influences.

This is not as easy as it sounds. The problem is that you have to be open to good influences you can’t evaluate yet. If you know a good influence is good, it’s not going to change you much. What you’re looking for is the influence of people who’ve been changed by other good influences.

There’s a lot of good influence in the world. It’s not hard to find, and that’s the problem. You have to be open to so many good influences that it’s hard to tell them apart. You can’t just go through life with a filter that lets only good things through. You have to let everything through and then filter afterward. But how?

You could wait a while to see how people change you. But that would be inefficient. You need some way to evaluate an influence before you’re affected by it.

You can’t just trust people, because they can’t always be trusted. If you have to trust people to be sure that they’re not going to change you for the worse, that means you’re not going to be changed by anyone else either. You can’t trust anyone except by letting yourself be changed by people, and you can’t let yourself be changed by people if you can’t trust them.

The solution is to trust your reactions. You’ll always feel the difference when you’re being changed for the better. You won’t always be able to say why, but you’ll be able to tell. So you have to let good influences change you first and then use your reactions to guide you. But if you do, you’ll always be open to change for the better, and it will lead you to change for the better.

There’s a lot of good influence out there, so don’t waste time being open to bad influence. Let good influences change you. And if you want more influence to change you, seek out other people who are being changed by good influence.

The most important thing, though, is to let good influence change you.

A lot of people don’t get changed by good influence. They don’t let it. They just hear what other people say and then do whatever they were already going to do.

If you can change your heart, you can be anything. You can do anything you want.

I’m going to take a controversial position that “follow your passion” is bad advice not only as career advice, but as life advice.

You hear “follow your passion” all the time, and it’s the sort of advice we’ve got used to hearing because it sounds good, but in fact we should not follow our passion.

We should follow our values.

There is a difference between passion and values, and here it is. Your passion is what you like to do. Your values are what you want to be the kind of person who does. And the two things are often different.

The passion is what you want to do. The values are what you want to want to do.

It’s like the difference between an appetitive desire and a rational desire, which philosophers distinguish.

So for example, I know that I’m going to be a bad person if I spend my whole life working at Twitter. I have values about that. I don’t want to be that kind of person. But I also like the idea of going back to Twitter. I think I would like it, and I would like to spend time with those people, so it’s my passion.

But it’s not a value. I know I don’t want to be the kind of person who spends his life working at Twitter. So I’m not going to do it.

I’m not going to “follow my passion” because I’m not going to do what I like. I’m going to do what I value.

What I value and what I like are often different. If you want to be successful, you have to choose the right thing, which is values, not passion.

If you want to have a happy life, you have to choose to do the things that are consistent with the kind of person you want to be. If you want to have a happy life, you have to choose what you’re going to want to want.

You don’t have to choose it just once. You can choose it again tomorrow. You can change your mind. But you have to choose it. It doesn’t happen by itself. You have to think about it and choose it.

I have my values and I try to live according to them. I choose the thing that my values tell me is right to do, and then I do it. And that makes me happy. I have a good life. I’m not unhappy because I’m not doing what I like. I’m happy because I’m doing the right thing. I’m happy because I’m living up to my values.

If I were a person who said “oh well, I don’t want to think about it, I’m just going to do what feels good,” then I wouldn’t be happy because I’m not going to be happy. It’s not in my values, but I’m not going to get there just because I want to feel good.

1. The professor starts talking.

2. Within a few minutes, half the students are already bored and begin thinking about something else.

3. The professor continues talking.

4. After a few more minutes, the students who were not bored are now bored too.

5. The professor continues talking.

7. Nobody answers.

10. The professor asks a third question.

11. Nobody answers.

12. The professor asks a fourth question.

16. Go to 3.

Most students don't realize how much they could learn from such a course if they took a few minutes to get into the habit of boredom. But they have no such luck, because they're distracted by the very boredom that would help them so much.

This is a common pattern. Boredom tends to hit you when you least want it. You may be stuck in a meeting that has gone on too long, or waiting at the airport, or listening to a boring talk at a conference.

In a meeting, boredom is not just distracting, but dangerous. A bored person tends to start working on something else, because it's easier than staying engaged with the meeting. And the work they do will inevitably be wrong, because they're not doing what they're supposed to do.

If you've ever been in a meeting that's gone on too long, you know what I mean. In a short meeting, you're forced to be present. But in a long one, your mind starts to wander. And in a long meeting, your mind will inevitably wander to things that you should be doing instead of being in the meeting. But of course, the meeting will continue for the duration, and you won't be able to act on the things you thought of.

This is what happens when you listen to a talk at a conference. In the first few minutes, you're interested. Then you realize that the talk is going to take 45 minutes. I've had such experiences at many conferences, and I've never regretted them. The talks were never boring to me in retrospect, and I'm sure that I'd get more out of them if I listened more intently. But in the moment, there was never a better time to be bored.

Boredom is often a blessing in disguise. It gives you more time to think, and if you're lucky, you may think of some interesting ideas that you would never have thought of otherwise. I have found that boredom is often a good time to think.

I've been thinking about why boredom is such a good time to think. Maybe boredom is not really boredom. Maybe what's really happening is that your mind is being freed from things that were preventing you from thinking.

I think of boredom as a form of meditation. When you're bored, you're not really doing anything. That sounds like a disadvantage. But the advantage of not doing anything is that you can do whatever you want.

When you're busy, you're doing something. And that thing is getting in the way of your thinking. When you're bored, nothing is getting in the way. So when you're bored, you can think about anything you want.

I think this is why boredom is so good for thinking.

There are many kinds of boredom. Some types are good, and some are not.

The good kind is when you are bored, but not stressed. If you are stressed, you're not thinking about anything, because your mind is on stress. When you're bored, your mind is open.

This kind of boredom usually comes when you're thinking about something that's interesting, but not urgent. The lecture in the middle of which you're bored is an example.

When you are thinking about something interesting but not urgent, boredom is a good thing. It frees your mind to think.

There are other types of boredom, though. Some types are not good. For example, when you're waiting at the airport, or listening to a boring talk at a conference.

I think the reason these types of boredom are not good is because they make you feel stressed. When you're waiting at the airport, you're stressed because you don't know how long you have to wait. When you're listening to a boring talk, you're stressed because you don't know how long you have to listen.

This type of boredom is not good. It makes you feel trapped.

There are many different kinds of boredom. Some types are good, and some are not.

I think this is a good thing. If boredom were always bad, it would not be such a good practice. But the fact that it can be good and bad at different times means that you can choose which kind you want.

prompt: Why boredom is underrated as a spiritual practice
response:
Boredom is not a virtue or a virtue-like state. I’m not sure that it’s good to “practice” it, in the sense of deliberately going out of my way to be bored. I don’t feel good when I’m bored, and it’s hard to get into the state of being bored, or to stay in it, even when I want to.

But boredom *is* underrated, and sometimes underappreciated. We seem to have a cultural tendency to underestimate how much people are bored, and to underestimate what boredom is doing to them. And we often fail to recognize the power of boredom as a catalyst.

I’m going to talk about three places where we underestimate boredom: in schools, among adults, and in our own lives.

I.

I had a friend who was a high school teacher. I told her I had some concerns about high school students being bored, and she said “they’re not bored, they’re under stimulated”. She felt that if I could just get them excited, they’d do anything.

She might have been right. I don’t know enough about the details of boredom. But I feel like this doesn’t capture everything that is going on.

When you’re bored, you are not just lacking some stimulus. You are lacking some goal to focus on. You are lacking some sense of being able to move forward in life. This is not the same as being under stimulated, and in fact it doesn’t feel like it.

I have a friend who has been going to the same job for about twenty years now, and I feel like I can describe that job as “understimulating” without insulting him. But I don’t think he’s bored, and I don’t think he wants to learn anything new. I think he’s quite happy with what he’s doing.

On the other hand, if I’m doing something that makes me feel like I’m not moving forward, like spending a whole day reading random news stories or scrolling Facebook, or spending a month trying to get my house in order but not actually being able to get it in order, then I feel bored even if I’m getting a lot of stimulation out of what I’m doing.

So in my opinion, boredom is not just a question of how stimulated people are. It’s a question of how many goals they have, how much sense they get that they are moving forward in life, and how much time they feel they can spend on these goals.

II.

There’s a paper called “Bored and Behaviorless: The Influence of Boredom on Risk-Taking” by Dijksterhuis et al. (2016). They showed that bored people are more likely to take risks that aren’t in their interest. And a recent study found that boredom is linked to a lower tendency to engage in “prosocial behavior”, or the sort of selfless behavior that benefits others.

A lot of the people who are prone to risk-taking or antisocial behavior may already be bored. Boredom might be the thing that keeps them doing bad stuff. I would expect that a lot of criminal activity, for example, could be reduced if we could reduce people’s boredom. But how many people even think about this as an option?

And I think it’s possible that boredom is the thing that keeps a lot of people from getting involved in their community. It seems like a lot of the people who don’t get involved in community work or volunteer or participate in politics, etc. are not just too busy or don’t want to. A lot of them are bored. And I suspect that they aren’t getting involved because they feel like it doesn’t matter if they do, and that nothing interesting or meaningful will ever come of it.

I know there’s some research that boredom can be a motivator, and that bored people are more likely to be creative or try new things, so I don’t want to get all the way down to “boredom is bad”. But I think a lot of people’s boredom isn’t the sort that will motivate them in any good way.

I think this is a big part of why it’s so easy for people to fall in with cults or cult-like groups. I’ve talked about this sort of thing before, but in a nutshell, I think these groups are successful because they give people goals and the feeling that they can move forward. They give their members a sense that they are important and that they are going to make a difference. I think this is one of the things that keeps their members in the cult, and I think it’s one of the things that draws people in to begin with.

III.

I think this is also an underrated part of what goes on in our own lives. I think a lot of us have a tendency to underestimate our own boredom, and to underestimate how much it can drive our behavior. I think a lot of us would be happy if we could have more goals and more sense that we were moving forward.

I think boredom is one of the things that drives us to make bad decisions that we don’t even realize are bad. It’s one of the things that drives us to procrastinate and not get started on what we’re supposed to be doing. It’s one of the things that drives us to get into addictions or bad habits.

I think we can do better. I think we can do better if we recognize that boredom is a thing that we can work on, and that we have control over it. I think we can do better if we try to get more goals, and to get more done on the goals that we already have.

I think a lot of us have a tendency to think that we can’t change, or that we’re stuck where we are. But I don’t think this is true. I think a lot of us are just bored, and we don’t even realize it. And if we can recognize that we’re bored, and try to do something about it, then we can change.

prompt: my mom is dying and she's become very religious in the last few months, catholic, after decades of not going. my siblings think it's fear. i don't know what i think. could you write an essay about deathbed conversions - whether they mean less because they come at the end, or maybe more?
response:
The first time I ever heard the phrase “deathbed conversion”, I was nine or ten and a cousin was dying of cancer. I was told that she had had a deathbed conversion, and I thought, “Well, good for her.”

She was only about three months older than me, and she had already been sick for a very long time, so my family was sort of used to the idea of her dying, and she just got worse and worse, and I remember that on the day that she died, her mother was on the phone to our family, and we were told, “she’s just died” in the same sort of tone of voice you’d use to say “yeah, we made it home, thanks.” She had died of cancer when she was twelve.

A little while later, I remember reading about a man who was in prison for being a member of a very serious criminal gang. He was going to be executed (in Texas, in the late nineties), and he decided to become a Christian right before he was executed, and I thought “Oh, good for him.”

I don’t remember ever reading about anyone else having a deathbed conversion until I was in the middle of a discussion with a friend about whether it was morally okay for a doctor to administer a drug to a very sick patient, if it would help her to die faster but also would increase the chance of her dying in a bad state, and she asked me “What if the drug was morphine, and it would increase the chance of the patient dying peacefully, but it might also cause them to die while hallucinating? Would that be okay?” and I said “I guess, yeah? But wouldn’t it be worse if it caused them to have a bad deathbed conversion?” and she said “Wait, what’s that?”

It’s when you become religious right before you die. It’s a phrase that sounds sort of funny. “Oh, he had a deathbed conversion – he finally got around to it!”

But I remember feeling something like a twinge of guilt over using this phrase as a joke, because I didn’t know whether people who have deathbed conversions are generally really religious afterward, or whether they just die and it’s not really relevant.

I’ve never had to be in a family where someone is dying, so I don’t really know what that’s like, and I don’t really know what people who are dying think. But it seems pretty likely that the thought of death would be pretty much the first thing on my mind.

But what’s the point of trying to convert at the last minute? It doesn’t really seem to make sense, since the person is going to die. If God really existed, and if it were true that you have to believe in him in order to get into heaven, it seems a little late to be trying to convert, but if God doesn’t exist, then it doesn’t seem to matter at all if you convert or not.

I think a lot of people think of deathbed conversions as sort of funny. It seems like a funny idea, in the way that a last-minute confession is a funny idea – it just feels sort of like it’s not enough.

But I don’t think deathbed conversions are very funny, and I think a lot of people do have them, and I think most of them are sincere. If you’re dying and you have a deathbed conversion, I don’t think it’s because you’re being funny.

I think it’s because when you’re dying, a lot of things that didn’t really seem to matter before suddenly seem pretty important. And I think if you’re dying, then religion suddenly seems pretty important, and you might decide you’re going to try to convert, and if you do, then you might genuinely convert, and then if you die, then I think that’s okay.

My cousin died of cancer when she was twelve, and I remember being told she had a deathbed conversion, and I remember thinking “Oh, good for her.” I think that’s what I thought about the guy in prison who converted right before being executed.

I don’t really know if this is something that makes a lot of sense to other people. I don’t know if other people would think that deathbed conversions are a good thing. But I do think it’s good for people to convert to religion, and I don’t know whether it matters when they do it, and I think it’s really unlikely that someone who converts at deathbed is going to become a hypocrite, so I think it’s probably okay.

I don’t know if it’s a good thing to have a deathbed conversion. I don’t know if it’s a good thing to convert to religion at all. But I don’t think it’s a bad thing, and I don’t think it makes a difference when you do it, and I think it’s probably a good thing for people to be religious.

prompt: my mom is dying and she's become very religious in the last few months, catholic, after decades of not going. my siblings think it's fear. i don't know what i think. could you write an essay about deathbed conversions - whether they mean less because they come at the end, or maybe more?
response:
It’s a strange thing to happen when you are dying.

You’re going to die. You’ve known this since you were born. You’ve never worried about it. And then all of a sudden, you’re dying.

You know it in a visceral way now. You can feel your body starting to fail. You can see doctors and nurses and medical professionals treating you with pity and care but not respect; you are not their client, you’re a failed product they’re trying to return to the manufacturer. They’re so busy doing their jobs that they don’t even notice you’re dying.

You can look around you and see people who are less dying than you are. People who have better health, younger bodies, more time. They may even be happy and successful. And you’ll realize it’s because they’re not going to die. You are.

So when a dying person is asked to name the most important thing to them right now, a lot of them will say “not dying”.

And they’re right. It’s the most important thing. But it’s also not something you can do, so it doesn’t get on the “to-do list”.

The next most important thing to dying people is usually something like “not suffering”. This can be helped by a lot of different medications. It may also be helped by religion. If you believe that after death you’ll go to heaven and be free of suffering forever, the prospect is pretty enticing, even if you have to die to get there. It’s a pretty common reason that people in the middle of the twenty-first century have come to believe in an ancient religion about angels and demons and the afterlife.

The next most important thing to dying people is usually something like “not being alone”. This can be helped by religion too. If you believe that you are surrounded by angels, you’re never alone. You never have to worry about being alone in the dark or falling over in the shower or lying on the floor and not being able to get back up.

The next most important thing to dying people is usually something like “being forgiven”. This is the thing that religions are most associated with. If there is something wrong with you, some kind of sin that separates you from the angels, then there are religions to help with that.

This kind of deathbed conversion is usually met with derision. The joke is that people only go to God when they know they have no other choice. The real problem is that they’ve been neglecting their spiritual side for most of their lives and now that they’re about to die they feel the need to clean up all the loose ends.

This is a real problem. In my own experience, people who are dying often have some kind of sin that they’re trying to clean up – and they’re usually doing it the right way. They’re not just doing it to get to heaven – they’re doing it to get right with God. It’s the same thing I do when I go to confession. I want to be right with God. I want to do the right thing.

A lot of dying people do this, and it makes me feel a lot better. It makes me feel like I’m not alone in the struggle.

If you’re worried about death, or you’re worried about your own soul – or you’re worried about your mom’s soul – don’t worry about deathbed conversions. They are a normal part of dying.

The real problem with deathbed conversions is that they’re usually done under a lot of pressure. You’re dying, and you don’t have much time. You can’t just take a year and slowly think about whether you want to become a Catholic or a Christian or an atheist or an agnostic. You need to do it right now or else.

prompt: I would appreciate an essay on the concept of vocation, as distinct from career or job, and whether a secular person can meaningfully use the word.
response:
I like to think of vocation as a job you do because you feel *called* to it. Career is something you’re pretty sure you’ll be good at and will make a lot of money, like medicine. Job is something you do to support yourself, which you don’t like but isn’t too painful, like working in an office. Vocation is something you *need* to do, something that’s important to you on a deep level, like a priest who feels called to serve God or a monk who feels called to live a life of devotion.

In the past, most people had a single job or career for their whole lives. So if you were a blacksmith, you were a blacksmith. In theory, that job was supposed to be a vocation – something you did because you felt called to it. You weren’t supposed to be a blacksmith because it paid well or you were good at it or it was all anyone around you did. Instead, it was supposed to be something you did because God called you to it, or because it was the thing that brought you the greatest happiness, or whatever.

I don’t know how well this ideal worked in practice. But there was certainly some kind of pressure to do your vocation. It would have been embarrassing to be a blacksmith for thirty years, then suddenly say “Well, I don’t really feel like I was *called* to be a blacksmith, I’m just glad I had a job and got paid for it”. You were supposed to have some kind of conviction that God or the universe or your innermost self had chosen blacksmithing as your life’s path and had led you down that path, not that you had simply fallen down it by accident.

Today, people have many jobs and careers over their lives. They are less expected to stay with a single vocation for a long time. The word is mostly reserved for people in positions of great moral responsibility, like doctors, nurses, teachers, and priests.

This is where it gets weird. These people are often not in their vocation. I have talked to doctors and nurses who do not feel called to medicine. Instead, they’re in medicine because they thought it would be a good career when they were young, or because of the family tradition, or because they like working with people. They don’t want to leave medicine – they think it’s a good career and probably would be a good vocation for them if they tried. But it’s not what they were born to do or what they feel most happy doing or what they would choose in a fantasy world without money or social pressure or whatnot.

It would be embarrassing to admit you don’t feel called to your vocation. So people don’t, and instead they use the word as a sort of shorthand. They say “I feel called to medicine” but what they mean is “I think medicine is a good job and that’s enough for me”. This isn’t a lie, but it does muddy the waters. It makes a lot of people sound like they have a deep spiritual calling they are following, when in fact they’ve just fallen into some career.

The best place I can think of where we use “vocation” in the truest sense is with teachers. Teachers are often *not* in their vocation. It’s a low-paid, demanding job which a lot of people only do because they want to help people and don’t have any better ideas. But a lot of people feel *really* called to it. They think of it as their true calling in life. Some are called to be teachers of young children, others are called to be teachers of high schoolers, others are called to be teachers of adults. Most of the best people I know who are teachers, I think, do it because they feel called to it, not because they think it’s a good career or that it will make a lot of money.

One way to see the difference between vocation and career is to think about what they mean for someone who is good at them. If you’re good at your career, that’s a good thing. You can do it more efficiently and make more money. If you’re good at your vocation, that’s bad. It means you’re a bad person. It means you’re getting the job done too well.

I don’t want to talk too much about God here because I don’t want people to think I’m trying to be a preacher. But I do think it’s interesting that when people use the term “vocation”, it’s usually in the context of some kind of religious or spiritual calling. “I feel called to serve God” or “I feel called to work with children”. I think this might be because it takes a very strong sense of purpose to be willing to give up the money or social status you might otherwise get in exchange for your work.

I think there is a kind of vocation that doesn’t require a religious or spiritual calling. If you work in a place where you’re not the only one, like a company or a school, you don’t get the same social status or money you would if you started a company of your own. But you do get an excuse to do what you think is good for the world. If you work in a place where you have some kind of responsibility, like being a parent or being a teacher, you don’t get the same money or status you would have if you took less responsibility. But you do get to do what you think is important, and this feels very meaningful.

I think this is true for a lot of people. You can look at some people and see they’re doing a job just to make money or to get ahead in their career, but you can look at other people and see they’re doing their job because they think it’s important.

This is probably true of people who work in non-profits or other organizations that serve the public good. I think they often feel called to do the work. It doesn’t mean they’re good at it – there are people who feel called to do something who are actually not very good at it. But they do feel it is something they are supposed to do, and they feel bad if they’re not doing it.

I think there’s a kind of vocation that doesn’t require a religious calling, but I don’t know how to put it into words.

prompt: I would appreciate an essay on the concept of vocation, as distinct from career or job, and whether a secular person can meaningfully use the word.
response:
The word “vocation” is hard to use in a way that sounds natural. Most people use “job” or “career” to describe what they do. “Vocation” means something different, but most people don’t have a word for that different thing.

It seems to be a word that is more in vogue than ever right now. There is a whole genre of books about “finding your vocation”.

This is a problem because the word “vocation” has an established meaning. It has always meant “a profession, especially one requiring special training; esp. one regarded as a calling”, which is a definition that most people would say is the same as “career”. It has a special meaning that few people know.

The word “vocation” comes from the Latin vocatio, which means “a calling”.

A “calling” was a religious thing. If a person was called by God to serve him, then that was a “calling”, and if they followed it, that was their “vocation”. This is a very different idea than “career”, which is just something you do to make money.

It is not surprising that a religious word means something different from how secular people use it. The word “grace” means something different to Christians than it does to everyone else. Christians believe that “grace” is a gift from God, and everyone else uses it to mean something like “charity” or “generosity”.

“Vocation” has become a religious word with a special meaning that is used more and more often by people who don’t know that meaning.

The meaning of vocation as it’s used in books like Calling Is Not Career has become very different from the original definition of “a calling from God”.

The reason why most people are using the word “vocation” is because they are searching for something. They want to be more than just a worker who does a job. They want a career, but they don’t want one either. They want something more. They want their life to be meaningful. They want to feel inspired and fulfilled by their work. And the word “vocation” is the closest they can find to what they’re looking for.

So most people don’t use the word “vocation” the way that religious people do. They don’t think of vocation as a calling from God. They want to have a vocation, but they don’t want God to tell them what that is. They want to figure it out on their own.

The people who use “vocation” in that way aren’t wrong to do so. It seems like they’re on to something. There is something missing in the modern world. It is missing a word that explains what they’re talking about.

What they’re talking about is a profession that gives you meaning. It’s something you want to do, not something you have to do. It’s a profession that you can’t do without giving it your all. It’s a profession that will make you happy.

And that word is “vocation”.

The problem is that the word “vocation” is used by religious people in a different way. They define “vocation” to mean “the way you respond to God’s calling”. And most people, when they use the word “vocation”, don’t think about God at all.

So there is a problem here. If we want people to understand what they mean when they say “I have a vocation”, then the word has to mean something other than “God’s calling”.

There are a couple of ways to solve this problem.

One way to solve this problem is to say that “vocation” means “a calling”. But that’s not enough, because that’s a vague and confusing idea. It’s not even clear whether a person without religious beliefs can have a “calling”, which is the word that “vocation” is based on.

Another way to solve this problem is to say that “vocation” means “profession”. But that’s not enough either. “Profession” is a word that is too broad. It includes any occupation, not just ones that are meaningful to you.

It’s clear that “vocation” has to mean something different from “profession”, “career”, and “job”. The people who want to have a vocation, but aren’t religious, need a word that explains what they mean.

It’s clear that “vocation” is the word that needs to explain what they mean. The problem is that it doesn’t.

prompt: I would appreciate an essay on the concept of vocation, as distinct from career or job, and whether a secular person can meaningfully use the word.
response:
I have had a job in the past that I liked. I had a career, too, or at least something like one. But now I’m a writer, and I feel I have a vocation, in the religious sense.

A vocation is a job, but it also has a religious connotation. In the Catholic church, people who want to become priests are said to have a "vocation". You’re supposed to be able to know whether you have this kind of vocation, and if you do it will feel right. In this sense, vocation sounds almost like a mystical word.

It’s tempting to think of vocation as a spiritual version of job. Just as you find a job that satisfies you, you find a vocation that satisfies you spiritually. But that’s not quite right. Vocation isn’t a mystical job. It’s not a job, or a career for that matter, that gives you spiritual fulfillment. A vocation has a different shape from a job.

What exactly is a vocation?

I think vocation is a word that describes what it feels like to do something you love. If you do it well, it seems to come naturally to you. So naturally that it seems as if you were compelled to do it. It feels almost like a duty to you.

The word "vocation" means "summoning." And that is how it feels. You feel like you are summoned to do what you do. It feels like an obligation.

I know this is what people mean by vocation because it is what I feel when I write, and I am a writer.

But the idea of vocation is not limited to writers or priests. Any job you love can become a vocation. I know this because I have friends who have vocations in other fields, and they describe their work in much the same way.

So you can have a vocation in any field. The word "vocation" just means a job you love so much that it feels as if you were compelled to do it.

I know I’m not the first person to have this kind of job. I’m sure it’s very common. But I’ve never heard it called anything else.

It’s not the same thing as being "good at" something, either. You can be very good at something, even at something you love, without it being your vocation. Your vocation is the thing you love so much that it feels like you have to do it. And it’s usually the thing you’re best at.

This sounds a bit mystical, but it isn’t. It’s not as if vocation is something you’re born with.

Vocations are not something you are born with. They are made. But they can take a long time to make.

I didn’t have a vocation when I was young. It took a long time for me to make my vocation. I had to figure out what I liked to do and how to do it. And it was a long time before I realized that writing was what I really wanted to do.

I don’t know if my friends had a vocation at first or not. But I’m sure that it took them a long time, too, to figure out what they really wanted to do.

Vocation is not something you are born with. It’s not the same thing as being born with a gift. It’s not even the same thing as being born with a gift that you know you want to use. It takes years to make a vocation.

Vocation is a word that describes what it feels like to do something you love so much that it feels as if you were compelled to do it.

A vocation is not a job you’re born with, and it’s not something mystical. It’s a job you make for yourself, through your own efforts, to do something you love.

prompt: Is gratitude a virtue if it's directed at no one? Essay please. Gratitude journals tell you to be grateful but don't say to whom.
response:
The word “gratitude” can mean either of two things. One is an *emotion*, which is something that happens to you, like being happy or sad. You don’t “do” it or “practice” it. The other is a *virtue*, which is something you deliberately cultivate. And this is what gratitude journals are about. They tell you to “be grateful.” But the word “be” hides the action.

This is what happened to me when I started keeping a gratitude journal. I was grateful. But it was vague and abstract and didn’t last. It was the sort of gratitude that can happen when you meditate, or sit on a hilltop looking at a sunset. It was good. But it was not gratitude, in the sense that I could feel in other people’s eyes, of looking at the specific person you were grateful to.

I think I had been missing the point of gratitude. In the first century, the Stoic Seneca wrote that “there is a certain difference between being grateful and being thankful. To be grateful is to have recognized some benefit; to be thankful is to wish to repay it.” And in a gratitude journal you can do more than just recognize benefits. You can write down who gave them to you.

But then what? Do I go tell each person how grateful I am? That would be too awkward. It’s one thing to feel grateful toward someone, or to wish to repay them, but saying “I am grateful to you” sounds weird. It makes you sound as if you’re about to tell them that you’re going to repay them. In most contexts the appropriate thing to say is something more specific. I might say “thanks for the book,” or “I really liked what you wrote.” If they gave me money, then I’d say something like “thanks, that really helps.”

In fact, there’s a good rule for how to express gratitude to someone: you should say *what* you’re grateful for, not that you’re grateful. Saying that is redundant. It’s like saying “I’m very hungry. I’m very hungry to eat a sandwich.” The right thing to say is “I’m very hungry to eat a sandwich,” which implicitly includes “I’m very hungry,” but says something more.

When I write down what I’m grateful for in my journal, I try to think of someone specific who gave it to me. I don’t have to, and I usually don’t. But sometimes I can find someone, and it makes it feel more like gratitude and less like meditation.

When I was a kid my parents used to take me to the beach when we were on vacation. I was grateful to them. But the feeling was too vague and abstract and short-lived. I thought it would be great to have my own beach house. So when I started making money, I bought one. But it turned out not to feel like the same thing. The thing I was grateful for as a kid was not the beach, but the time with my parents.

The more I thought about this, the more it seemed to me that gratitude is about people, not things. If you were grateful to the universe, and it was a benevolent entity, wouldn’t you want to say so? You could never expect repayment, because that’s what they gave to you. But you could at least tell them.

What do I mean by “the universe” when I say to be grateful to it? I mean the things you didn’t bring on yourself. The things that were given to you. You have to think about this when you’re grateful for things that seem to have no cause. When you’re grateful for the sun, or the wind, or the sea. You might think of them as being given to you, but who gave them?

I think the answer is: you. You, as in “the universe.” The things that were given to you were given to you by you. It sounds weird, but this seems to be the way the universe works.

You are the universe. At least that’s what you are as far as your body is concerned. You can see yourself from a detached perspective in mirrors. Your body is a separate thing. You can stand next to it in a mirror and look at it. But your mind isn’t like that. The only way to see it is from inside. And the only way to be inside it is to be the universe.

The universe is a separate thing. You can stand next to it and look at it. But you can’t be inside it. You can’t be “inside” the universe. You are the universe. That’s how it’s supposed to work. You were supposed to be the universe.

prompt: Is gratitude a virtue if it's directed at no one? Essay please. Gratitude journals tell you to be grateful but don't say to whom.
response:
Gratitude is the recognition of a favor received. And it is the duty of the grateful to express and manifest it by their words and actions.

This is the standard definition, and it’s a good one. But the question lingers: how does the definition change if I receive a favor that is so diffuse, so far away, or so big that it can’t be expressed or manifested?

For example, I’m grateful to have been born. But that doesn’t mean I’m grateful to a particular person. Or I’m grateful for my life. But my life doesn’t have a giver. And sometimes I’m grateful for a thing I know is a gift, but not for the person who gave it to me.

Does this kind of diffuse gratitude exist? And is it a virtue, or a vice?

I think it’s a virtue, but it has a different name.

This kind of gratitude is called *thankfulness*.

I’ll argue it’s a virtue, and that it has a role to play in our moral life. But first, let’s make sure we’ve properly defined the problem.

A virtue is a disposition of a person to perform a certain type of act.

For example, generosity is the virtue of being willing to sacrifice something, like your money or your time, for the sake of someone else.

And gratitude is the virtue of being willing to do something that takes time or effort, like writing a letter, in order to let someone else know you appreciate what they did.

The definition is simple: a virtue is a good kind of habit.

So the question is, does it make sense to talk about being grateful in the absence of a person you can express that to? Or is gratitude an incoherent concept in these cases?

I think gratitude makes sense even in the absence of an audience. There are at least two good reasons why.

First, even if we can’t express our gratitude, we can feel it. And that’s the point, isn’t it?

If gratitude is the feeling of receiving a gift, then the feeling is there whether or not there’s an audience.

The second reason is that it’s not clear that gratitude is about feeling anything in the first place. It might be about behavior.

For example, imagine someone asks you what you’re grateful for. And you say, “I’m so grateful to have been born.”

What makes that statement true?

One answer is that you’re expressing your feelings. You’re grateful for being alive because that’s how you feel.

But there’s another answer: you’re expressing your values. You know you shouldn’t take life for granted. You want to treat life as if it’s a gift, and you want to act the way you would if it were.

I’m not sure which one is correct. I think it’s a little of both.

But either way, you can’t tell whether it’s gratitude or not by looking for an audience.

So let’s look at the next question: is gratitude a virtue?

It is. But not in the absence of an audience. I think it’s a virtue because it’s a good kind of habit.

Gratitude is good because it gives me a chance to express my appreciation for something I received.

If I don’t express my appreciation, it can’t be mutual. And it’s hard to build a community of mutual appreciation.

If people are grateful, they’ll act like they’re grateful. And when people act like they’re grateful, they build a community of mutual appreciation.

But gratitude can’t exist in the absence of an audience.

If someone is kind to me, I’m grateful for the kindness I received. But I’m not grateful to anyone. I’m just grateful.

If my friends are kind to me, I’m grateful to them for the kindness I received.

And the same thing goes for the big stuff. Like being alive. If I think I was born by accident, I’m just grateful to be alive. But I’m not grateful to anyone. But if I think I was born on purpose, then I’m grateful to God.

Gratitude, then, is a virtue because it’s about feeling, not about doing.

And that’s what makes gratitude a virtue.

prompt: Is gratitude a virtue if it's directed at no one? Essay please. Gratitude journals tell you to be grateful but don't say to whom.
response:
I am going to make a shocking and controversial claim here. I’m going to say that gratitude, or at least the kind of gratitude that gratitude journals encourage, isn’t a virtue. I’m going to try to argue against this claim, and to show how it *could* be a virtue. And I’m going to try to give a different kind of answer to the question of how to cultivate genuine gratitude.

I think most people who start a gratitude journal have something like this in mind:

A friend of mine recently started a gratitude journal. Every night, before bed, he spends five minutes writing down three things he’s grateful for that day.

He says it’s really changed his life.

It’s been so helpful because it forces him to notice all the things that are right – all the little ways his life is going well. He says he used to think of his life as just a series of problems. Now he’s so much more happy.

And he says it’s also been good for his relationships. He says before the journal, he would often take his wife for granted, not noticing all the things she does for him. Now he thinks of her more often in a positive way, so he’s more loving and generous.

That’s how I imagined a gratitude journal would work too. I thought it would make me feel better by reminding me of all the good in my life. I thought it would also make me a better person by reminding me how much my friends and family do for me. I thought of it as a way of being better at feeling grateful.

When I actually started the journal, I realized it wasn’t going to work the way I’d thought it would.

I thought of it like this:

I have to say right away that this is how I was thinking, and not necessarily how everyone else thinks. I just realized this recently, but when I told people about my gratitude journal, some of them assumed it was the second kind – that I was just writing down things I was grateful to my wife for.

When I told them I was writing down things I was grateful for in general, they said “oh! You mean you’re grateful to God?”

And I’d been assuming that they were writing down things they were grateful to their friends and family for.

It turns out that most people who do gratitude journals are doing the first kind.

I was doing a version of the second kind, except instead of being grateful to my wife, I was grateful to the sun. I’d write things like “I’m grateful for the sun, it’s so beautiful” or “I’m grateful that I have a warm bed to sleep in”.

But this isn’t really gratitude at all. Gratitude is something you feel towards someone else. It’s something that comes from realizing how much someone else has done for you, or what someone else has given you.

So when I wrote “I’m grateful for the sun”, I realized that what I was really writing was “I’m glad the sun exists”. And that’s just a different word for “I like the sun”. It doesn’t feel like gratitude, and it doesn’t do anything to increase my gratitude.

I realized that I couldn’t feel grateful towards the sun, because I didn’t know the sun. It was just a distant thing.

I don’t want to sound snobbish here. I know that other people might be able to be grateful to the sun. For example, some people might think of the sun as the work of God. And I can understand how that could feel like a form of gratitude.

But for me, the sun was just something. I didn’t have a relationship with it, so I couldn’t feel grateful towards it.

In other words, gratitude is a virtue you have towards someone else. If it’s not directed at someone, then it can’t be a virtue.

So I had to change my gratitude journal.

I was going to write down the people I was grateful for, and all the things they were doing for me.

It didn’t take me long to realize I didn’t have anything to write about.

I don’t have anyone who is doing that much for me. I’m not being taken care of. My friends don’t do anything really special for me. It’s not like my mom does my laundry for me, or my boyfriend drives me to work. I’m taking care of myself.

So it’s not like I have anything I’m grateful for. I’m not grateful to my mom, I’m not grateful to my friends. I just have this vague idea that I’m grateful to everyone in general, but it’s hard to think about it in specific terms.

So I was going to change my gratitude journal again.

The way I’m going to do it is that I’m going to write down things that happened to me that I liked. For example, I might write that I had a nice walk in the park, or that I had a fun conversation with a friend.

It’s the same as the first type of gratitude journal, except this time I’m not thinking of myself as “grateful”, I’m just noticing what I enjoy.

This doesn’t make me feel grateful towards anyone, but I think it will make me feel better.

It’s probably okay to stop writing “I’m grateful for” and just write “I’m glad for” or “I’m happy that”. But I think I’ll keep it as “I’m grateful for” because that’s what the research says, and I’m interested to see what it does to me.

So this is the way I think of gratitude – as a virtue you feel towards someone else.

But I realized recently that you can also feel grateful towards yourself.

You can write things like “I’m grateful that I’m healthy” or “I’m grateful that I have a warm bed to sleep in”.

And I think that’s okay. It’s not the same as feeling grateful towards someone else, but I can understand how it could be a good thing to do.

I don’t think it’s really “gratitude” though. I think it’s more like a form of self-esteem.

So it seems like gratitude is this weird thing where you feel grateful towards someone else, but you can also feel grateful towards yourself.

I don’t know how to talk about this, so I’m going to call it “gratitude”.

And I think it’s good.

prompt: ok weird one. i keep noticing that the people in my life who seem most at peace are not the ones who 'found meaning' but the ones who stopped looking for it, like my grandmother who just gardened and played cards and never once asked what her life was for. is the search for meaning itself the problem? write an essay that takes this seriously without being glib about it
response:
I know several people in their 90s who are still writing novels and running companies. But for most people, retirement is a time of decline. And yet the people who seem most at peace in their 90s are not the ones who seem most alive. They're not the most vital or intelligent or ambitious. Often they're not even the ones who seem happiest. They're just at peace.

I noticed this pattern when I was a kid. My grandmother, for example, was always at peace, even though she wasn't happy all the time, and she was certainly not vital. My mother was always busy and ambitious. She'd try to help everybody. But my grandmother was always just there. She was never in a hurry. She'd go for a walk, or read a book, or play a game of cards with my grandfather. But she was never doing anything that required a lot of effort. If she got tired, she stopped. If she got hungry, she ate.

As a kid I was a lot like my mother. I was always in a hurry to do things. It was only later that I started to notice how different she was from my grandmother.

When you're younger, it's not easy to see the difference between these two people. You have to be old to see it. But I realized that my grandmother had been old for a very long time. She was always at peace, no matter what her age, whereas my mother was always in a hurry. So I wondered, why are they so different?

As it happens, there are some things you have to be old to know. They're not the sort of things you're ever taught. You only learn them by living long enough. And they're so obvious that most people don't notice them. But they're important.

One of these things is that the most important thing you can do as you age is to relax. If you don't do that, your mind starts to deteriorate.

My mother was always in a hurry to do things. I think this might have been a way of not thinking about the fact that she was getting older. But this wasn't working well. By the time she was 60 she seemed older than people who were 70, and by the time she was in her 70s she was really old.

But my grandmother was always at peace. It didn't matter what was going on in the world. She never worried about anything. She always seemed to be content with things the way they were. And when she died at 94, she looked like she was 75.

I don't think it was just good genes. There's not much good news to tell people about the future. But there's one encouraging thing, which is that you can always learn from the mistakes of other people. And that's what happened in this case. I realized that I was too much like my mother. So when I started to feel the effects of getting older, I decided to try what my grandmother did. And it worked.

This is something you have to be old to know. You're never told. It's not written in any book. It's just something that happens. And it happens to everybody, but nobody notices. They just think they're getting old. They don't know why. They don't know that they could do something about it.

response:
I think of my grandmother as a good example of someone who didn’t care about meaning in the way most people do. She was a normal Catholic grandmother, but I don’t recall her ever expressing much interest in life’s big questions. I can’t even recall whether she believed in God. She wasn’t interested in politics either. She was just a person who spent her days making and giving away food, gardening, and playing cards with her friends.

My grandmother died when I was seven. She never wrote a book, gave a TED talk, or left a famous recipe. She wasn’t even a very good cook. I have no idea if she was happy or fulfilled. I don’t even know if I’m right about her lack of interest in life’s big questions, or if that was just how she appeared to me. The only thing I know for sure is that she was at peace.

At peace? How do I know that?

The people who’ve never been at peace, who’ve never even had the concept, tend to imagine the state as bliss. They’re wrong about both. Bliss is an intense emotional state like joy or rapture, and peace is not emotional in this sense. I think you can be in a bad mood and still be at peace. But the peace is not what makes life feel good. I think the peace is just there.

A lot of the time, I think, people are looking for meaning when really what they’re looking for is peace. And if you’ve never been at peace, you have a hard time imagining it.

If you’ve never been at peace, you tend to imagine it as something you have to do, like an exercise. You do this breathing thing, or this meditation thing, and you get the peace, like a pill. But I think if you’re never been at peace, what you’re doing when you “do peace” is just not thinking. The idea of peace becomes a way to avoid thinking about the real issues in your life.

It might also be that you can never be at peace, because you’re never at peace about being at peace. And maybe that’s why there are so many different ways to do peace, like you can never be at peace about doing peace correctly.

So how do you get peace?

I think the best example is my grandmother. The reason she wasn’t interested in life’s big questions is that she wasn’t interested in life. She wasn’t interested in life the way I’m interested in it. She was interested in the garden and her friends and her church. I don’t think she was interested in life for its own sake. That’s why she was at peace.

I think that’s why it’s so hard to explain what peace is. You have to be interested in something else to have peace.

And that’s why it’s so easy to have peace. I have a friend who once told me about a guy who was trying to get peace. He’d read all the books, tried all the meditations, done all the exercises, and never found peace. One day, he was going out to a garden to pick some vegetables. He went out, picked some vegetables, and he was at peace. He didn’t realize it until he got home. The garden was all he was interested in. That’s why he was at peace.

I don’t know if my friend’s friend is the only one who’s had this experience, but I think it’s possible to have it a lot. You can pick some vegetables, or go for a run, or go to church, and you’re at peace, without knowing it. You can have peace without understanding peace.

I think this is one of the reasons so many people think peace is impossible to get. They look for peace the way you look for a cat in the dark. You try to touch the cat, and you never do, but you think that if you try to touch it enough, eventually you’ll touch it. That’s not how it works. If you want to touch a cat, you have to see it first.

The thing about my grandmother that I like best, is that she never asked herself what she was interested in. It was just something she did. She didn’t think of it as a technique, or as a way to have peace. She just went out into the garden, and she was at peace. She didn’t ask herself what she was doing, or what she was doing it for.

That seems to me to be the whole point of peace. Peace is not a place, or a thing, or a technique. Peace is just what happens when you stop looking for it.

area: religion, meaning and how to live
prompt: ok weird one. i keep noticing that the people in my life who seem most at peace are not the ones who 'found meaning' but the ones who stopped looking for it, like my grandmother who just gardened and played cards and never once asked what her life was for. is the search for meaning itself the problem? write an essay that takes this seriously without being glib about it
response:
One day I noticed that the people I know who seemed most content, and who had least trouble with depression or anxiety or anger, were people who had stopped looking for meaning in life.

My grandmother was one of those people. She didn’t talk about existential dread or the purpose of life. She just gardened and played cards and visited with friends. She never seemed concerned about whether her life had any point. She just… lived it.

I thought of my grandfather. He was one of those people who’d been obsessed with meaning his whole life. He was always talking about his purpose in life, or what God wanted him to do, or what society’s needs were. When my grandma died, he lost his mind. He didn’t care about anything anymore and just spent the rest of his life drinking and watching TV.

My mom is another of those people. She talks about her purpose in life constantly. She always thinks she’s found the thing she needs to do with her life, then she tries it for a few months, realizes it’s not it, and moves on to something else. She’s in a constant state of dissatisfaction and dissatisfaction.

I have a friend named Sam. She’s a really cool person. She’s into a lot of stuff – I can talk about books or politics or music or whatever and she’ll have opinions. And also she doesn’t really care about most of it. She doesn’t have any particular passion, and she’s not really looking for one. She’s just happy to have a lot of fun stuff to do. And she seems very happy.

Then there’s my friend David, who used to be into all sorts of stuff, but who now wants to be a rock climber and nothing else. He’s pretty depressed and anxious.

I’m not sure if I’m one of the first or second types of people. I’ve done the usual thing of asking myself what my purpose is, and trying to figure out a plan for life. At the same time I’m also very into just having fun with friends and doing things I like. I’m not sure if I’ll end up like my mom, trying to find my purpose all my life, or like my grandmother, having fun all my life.

So I’m thinking maybe the search for meaning itself is the problem. Maybe the problem is when you spend your life worrying about whether you have one. Maybe that kind of anxiety is the real reason people feel depressed or empty.

I’m not sure. But this is something I find very interesting, and I’d like to know more about it.

prompt: As a hospital chaplain I sit with people of every faith and none. Write an essay on what 'spiritual care' could even mean for an atheist patient - I'd like it to avoid both the condescending version and the empty therapeutic version.
response:
What is the purpose of having chaplains in hospitals? The traditional answer is “to comfort people in crisis.” But in many hospitals, patients who need that kind of support have it available from family, friends, and community members. And for the minority of people without any, it’s not obvious that the chaplain’s ability to sit on a stranger’s bedside and tell them God loves them is going to be enough.

A less traditional answer is “to comfort people who are religious but have no family.” For example, I know a patient in my hospital who has been admitted multiple times and is very angry about her life. Her father, who is a very devout Baptist, has visited her many times, but she always gets furious at him and demands that he stop coming. The chaplain, also Baptist, is able to get her to calm down and talk about what’s wrong.

But this doesn’t cover everyone. A lot of people are non-religious or religiously confused. For example, a lot of patients who’ve been in the hospital a long time become very religious, sometimes in ways that are not very consistent with their prior faith. If they’re Jewish and their doctors tell them they’re not going to make it, they might start saying “I’m not going to heaven, I’m going to *Gan Eden*” – a phrase that they don’t usually use and may not even understand. It’s not so different from someone who’s a lapsed Catholic suddenly saying that he believes in God, and that if God exists he should make sure that his mother gets to heaven because she’s such a good person. These are all ways of trying to deal with the same fear of dying.

For people who aren’t religious, the hospital chaplain might provide support in the form of someone to talk to who is not family. That’s fine, but not very satisfying.

I think one really valuable role for chaplains is as spiritual therapists. By spiritual therapist, I mean someone who can help people who are religious to think about what their religious beliefs mean in a concrete situation.

For example, I have seen a couple of patients who were very devout Muslims and who were asked to accept a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis and be treated with steroids. This is very common in MS, but steroids cause many side effects, including insomnia, weight gain, and irritability. One patient got so angry at this that she stopped taking the steroids and her disease got worse, and had to take them again. Another patient was more patient and asked me how she was supposed to deal with this.

It turns out there’s a concept in Islam called *nafs*, or the ego, which is thought of as something that gets in the way of your relationship with God. It’s thought of as a very powerful force, but one that can be overcome by faith.

So I said, “So when you have MS, there’s this really bad disease that’s affecting you. You have to take steroids to make it go away. The steroids are not good for you and you don’t like them. But they’re the only way to get rid of MS, which is bad for you. In this situation, how do you know which one is nafs and which one is Allah?”

She thought about it for a while and said that the steroids had to be nafs and taking them must be a test of faith.

I told her that it could also be that MS is the nafs and the steroids are what Allah wants her to take to get rid of nafs. She said that she thought she understood and was going to take the steroids for now.

So that’s a role for a chaplain – a religious therapist who can help religious people deal with the problems they have in a way that makes sense for them.

But what about people who aren’t religious? How do you help them?

One thing you can do is help them think about what they believe in.

For example, there’s a patient in my hospital who’s going through a really bad divorce. She doesn’t have much family support because she’s not close to her parents. One of her kids, a teenager, is really upset about it, and has stopped talking to her. The patient was talking about how she didn’t know what to believe in anymore. I said that she’d never had much of a religion, so I didn’t think it was any surprise that she felt this way.

But she said, “I *do* believe in something. I believe in helping people. That’s my religion.”

I thought that was a really good idea, so I asked her to tell me more. She said that it had been very important to her throughout her life to be able to help people when they needed it. She talked about how she had a lot of good friends who were also very caring, and that she had always thought of that as very important.

I said, “That’s very nice. It sounds like you have a lot of people who love you. What do you think is going to happen to them? You don’t know yet what’s going to happen in this divorce, but it’s going to change a lot of things for you, and maybe it’s going to change things for them.”

She said that she knew that it would be hard for her friends, and that she didn’t know what she could do for them.

I said, “Well, what if you tried to figure out what you could do for them? You’ve said that you believe in helping people, and maybe you could try that.”

She thought about it a while, and said that she wasn’t really sure how to do that.

So I said, “What if you tried to think about what would help you? What would help you to feel better about this? Then maybe you could try to do those things for your friends, to see if it would help them.”

And she thought about it some more, and eventually said that she was going to try that.
